jurisdictions.label: Mauritius
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator of Vacant Estates
jurisdictions.summary: A standing public office rather than a per-estate appointment. The Curator administers all vacant estates on the Attorney-General’s directions, and also administers the estates of minors or adults that the Judge in Chambers vests in him under the Code Civil.

assigned.event: Estate falls vacant, or the Judge in Chambers vests the estate of a minor or adult in the Curator under the Code Civil

starts.event: The Curator administers the estate on the Attorney-General’s directions, exercising his powers as he thinks best in the interests of those entitled

ends.event: Administration completed and the estate distributed to those entitled

jurisdictions.label: Rwanda
jurisdictions.roleName: Liquidator
jurisdictions.summary: Rwanda does not leave the estate to the heirs to settle between themselves. After the succession opens a liquidator is appointed, chosen and supervised by the succession council — from among the heirs if possible — which sets the deadline for the work and must approve what the liquidator has done.

assigned.event: After the opening of succession a liquidator is appointed; the succession council chooses and supervises them, from among the heirs if possible, and sets the deadline for discharging the role

starts.event: The liquidator liquidates the estate and presents and determines the procedure for repayment of the inherited debts

ends.event: On completion the liquidator reports to the succession council, which approves the acts performed

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor dative
jurisdictions.summary: Where nobody was nominated by will, or the nominee cannot be found or will not act, the Master appoints. On intestacy the estate then devolves under the Intestate Succession Act.

assigned.event: Master acts where there is no nomination, or the nominee's whereabouts are unknown, or they have died, are incapacitated or refuse to act

starts.event: Master issues letters of executorship

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed to those entitled

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Estate administrator (遗产管理人)
jurisdictions.summary: An office the 2021 Civil Code created outright. Once succession opens the executor is the administrator; if there is none the heirs must promptly elect one, and if they do not elect they serve jointly. Where there are no heirs, or all renounce, the civil affairs department or the villagers’ committee of the decedent’s last domicile serves. Where the choice is disputed an interested party may ask the court to designate.

assigned.event: Succession opens; the executor is the administrator, failing which the heirs elect or serve jointly, failing which the civil affairs department or villagers’ committee serves

starts.event: The administrator clears the estate and makes an inventory, reports to the heirs, prevents loss, deals with the decedent’s debts and claims, and divides the estate

ends.event: The duties in art 1147 are discharged, ending with division of the estate
An interested party applies to the People’s Court, which designates a different administrator where the choice is disputed

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator
jurisdictions.summary: Where there is no executor, administration may be granted to any person who would be entitled to the whole or part of the estate. Like the executor, the administrator is the legal representative and the property vests in them.

assigned.event: Court grants administration to a person entitled to the whole or any part of the deceased’s estate

starts.event: On the grant of letters of administration; the administrator is legal representative for all purposes

ends.event: Administration of the estate completed

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator
jurisdictions.summary: On intestacy the court may grant letters of administration, having regard to the rights of everyone interested in the estate. Where security is required it is ordinarily a bond by the grantee and two sureties in the sworn amount of the estate.

assigned.event: Person dies intestate and the court considers the rights of all persons interested in the estate

starts.event: On the grant of letters of administration, subject to any security the registrar requires

ends.event: Administration of the estate completed

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator of an estate with no known heir
jurisdictions.summary: Where it is unknown whether an heir exists, the court appoints an administrator of the inherited property on the application of a relative or other interested party.

assigned.event: Court appoints an administrator on application, where it is unknown whether an heir exists

starts.event: On appointment by the court

ends.event: An heir is found and accepts, or the administration is completed

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Bobestyrer
jurisdictions.summary: The probate court releases the estate to an authorised administrator where an heir asks, the estate looks insolvent, the heirs cannot act, or the heirs are unknown.

assigned.event: Skifteretten releases the estate to a bobestyrer

starts.event: On release of the estate

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Pesänselvittäjä

citation.cite: Code of Inheritance 40/1965 ch 19 s 1 (amendments up to 1228/2001)
citation.title: Code of Inheritance (unofficial translation published on Finlex)
citation.quote: the court shall order that the property of the estate is to be surrendered to the administration of an estate administrator

jurisdictions.summary: On an estate party's application the court orders the estate handed to an administrator and appoints someone to run it.

assigned.event: Court appoints on application of a party to the estate

starts.event: On the court's decision

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Nachlasspfleger

citation.title: Act on Proceedings in Family Matters and in Matters of Non-contentious Jurisdiction (official English translation, as amended to 7 April 2025)
citation.quote: curatorship of the estate or administration of the estate include the curator of the estate or the administrator of the estate

jurisdictions.summary: Where the heir is unknown or has not yet accepted, the probate court secures the estate and may appoint a curator for whoever turns out to be the heir.

assigned.event: Nachlassgericht appoints where there is a need to secure the estate

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Heir established and accepts the estate

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator
jurisdictions.summary: Where there is no executor, nobody holds the estate in the interval after death: it vests in the President of the High Court as a corporation sole until administration is granted.

assigned.event: Person dies intestate, or testate leaving no surviving executor

starts.event: High Court grants administration, with or without will annexed; until then the estate is vested in the President of the High Court as a corporation sole

ends.event: Administration completed, or the grant revoked, cancelled or recalled by the High Court

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator of a vacant estate (curatore dell’eredità giacente)
jurisdictions.summary: Where the person called to the estate has not accepted and does not hold estate assets, the court appoints a curator, on application or of its own motion. The curator inventories the estate, pursues and answers claims, and may pay the estate’s debts and legacies with the court’s authorisation. The office ends the moment the estate is accepted.

assigned.event: The person called has not accepted and is not in possession of estate assets; the court of the district where succession opened appoints a curator, on application by interested persons or of its own motion

starts.event: The curator inventories the estate, exercises and pursues its claims, answers claims brought against it, and administers it

ends.event: The curator ceases to act the moment the estate is accepted

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: Boutredningsman

citation.cite: Government Offices of Sweden, Death and inheritance (published 8 April 2025)
citation.title: Estate of a deceased person
citation.quote: If the part owners disagree, an estate administrator (boutredningsman) can administer the estate and deal with any administrative difficulties.

jurisdictions.summary: Appointed by the court on a party's request to take over administration of the estate from the joint owners.

assigned.event: Court appoints on request of a dödsbodelägare

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator
jurisdictions.summary: If there is no will, or no executor who can prove it, someone must be granted letters of administration, in the order of priority set by the Non-Contentious Probate Rules 1987 (r 22 for intestacy, r 20 for a will). An administrator has no authority until the grant. Until then the estate vests in the Public Trustee. Once granted, the administrator's title relates back to the date of death.

assigned.event: Probate registry grants letters of administration to the person entitled under NCPR r 20/r 22 (or court appoints under SCA 1981 s 116)

starts.event: On the grant (title then relates back to the death for property, but not to validate proceedings begun earlier)

ends.event: Estate fully administered; no formal discharge
Grant revoked by the court

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator (letters of administration)
jurisdictions.summary: Where there is no will, or no executor able or willing to act, the Probate Office grants letters of administration in a statutory order of priority: surviving spouse, children or their issue, parents, siblings or their issue, then remoter kin. Before the grant, an intestate's estate vests in the Probate Judge.

assigned.event: Probate Office issues letters of administration to highest-priority applicant

starts.event: On the grant

ends.event: Estate distributed

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor-dative (appointed by the sheriff)
jurisdictions.summary: Where there is no executor-nominate (usually intestacy), a person such as the surviving spouse or civil partner or next of kin petitions the sheriff to be appointed executor-dative. They then obtain confirmation, usually with a bond of caution. For small estates, the sheriff clerk handles it without a separate petition or caution.

assigned.event: Sheriff decerns the petitioner executor-dative (large estate). For a small intestate estate, the sheriff clerk prepares the inventory and expedes confirmation without caution.

starts.event: On confirmation, which vests the estate for administration

ends.event: Estate ingathered and distributed
Confirmation becomes inoperative on death or incapacity of all executors

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator (grant of administration, with or without will annexed)
jurisdictions.summary: If there is no will, or no executor who can or will act, the court grants administration by statutory priority. For intestacy the order is spouse, then a child with the consent of a majority of children, then other intestate successors, then anyone the court considers appropriate, including the PGT. An intestate administrator is deemed personal representative from the date of death.

assigned.event: Court grants administration following the s 130 or s 131 priority list, or special-circumstances appointment

starts.event: On issue of the grant (estate vests in the court until then); for intestacy the administrator is conclusively deemed personal representative from the date of death

ends.event: Grant revoked, or administrator removed
Court discharge

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Estate trustee without a will (administrator)
localNames: certificate of appointment of estate trustee without a will
jurisdictions.summary: If a person dies intestate, or the named executor refuses to prove the will, the Superior Court may commit administration to the married or conjugal spouse, the next of kin, or both, at its discretion. With the consent of the majority of those entitled, it may appoint another person. The administrator's authority comes from the court certificate. A bond is generally required, but not for small estates without minor or incapable beneficiaries.

assigned.event: Court issues a certificate of appointment of estate trustee without a will (or a small estate certificate)

starts.event: On issuance of the certificate

ends.event: Court removes the administrator
Estate fully administered and accounts passed or approved

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Liquidator by operation of law (the heirs) or designated by the heirs or court
jurisdictions.summary: If no liquidator is designated by will, including on intestacy, the office devolves by law to the heirs together. A majority of heirs may designate a liquidator. If the sole heir is a minor or an adult under tutorship or a protection mandate, the representative designates someone else. The court designates or replaces a liquidator when heirs disagree or no one can be appointed. There is no grant of administration.

assigned.event: By operation of law at the opening of the succession (heirs), or designation by majority of heirs, or court designation

starts.event: Opening of the succession (death)

ends.event: Court replacement
Final account accepted; discharge

jurisdictions.label: Mexico — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Albacea electo por los herederos o nombrado por el juez

nameEn.en: Executor elected by the heirs or appointed by the judge

jurisdictions.summary: Where the testator named no albacea, or the one named does not serve, the heirs elect one by majority; if there is no majority the judge appoints from those proposed. The same applies on intestacy.

assigned.event: Heirs elect by majority, or the judge appoints from those proposed

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Accounts rendered and the office discharged

jurisdictions.roleName: DWP appointee

assigned.event: Secretary of State (DWP) appoints on written application, after DWP checks that the claimant is unable to act and the applicant is suitable (form BF56, confirmed by BF57)

starts.event: On formal appointment (BF57 issued); not before

ends.event: Secretary of State revokes the appointment (e.g. appointee not acting properly, or claimant can manage own benefits)
Appointee resigns with one month's written notice

DWP is notified that a Court of Protection deputy (or Scottish guardian/judicial factor) with power over benefits exists; for UC, PIP, new-style JSA/ESA, also a registered attorney with a general or benefits power
Claimant dies. The regulations do not expressly say so: reg 33/57 cover a living person 'unable to act', and after death a separate appointment under reg 30 is needed to proceed with a claim

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Trustee for CPP / OAS benefits of an incapable beneficiary
localNames: person or agency to whom the benefit is paid on behalf of a beneficiary
jurisdictions.summary: If the Minister is satisfied that a beneficiary is incapable of managing their own affairs, CPP or OAS benefits can be paid to a person or agency on the beneficiary's behalf. That is a legally authorized manager (such as a provincial attorney or guardian) or, failing one, a person or agency the Minister approves who signs an agreement to administer the benefits. The trustee must account and must return payments issued after the month of death.

assigned.event: Minister is satisfied, on medical or other evidence (in practice a Certificate of Incapability, ISP-3505), that the beneficiary cannot manage their own affairs, and directs payment to a legally authorized person or agency or, if none, to a Minister-approved person or agency

starts.event: Once the person or agency has signed the agreement to administer the benefits (ISP-3506 private / ISP-3507 agency). Under the CPP Regulations, no benefit may be paid to them until they do.

ends.event: Beneficiary dies: CPP retirement and OAS pensions stop with the payment for the month of death, and the trustee must return uncashed payments and any issued after that month
Beneficiary stops being incapable of managing their own affairs: the trustee must notify ESDC, and the legal basis for a direction under s 55 / s 24 falls away
ends.note: Neither regulation has an express revocation clause. The end on regaining capacity is inferred from the incapacity precondition and from the notice duty in the ISP-3506 undertaking.

ends.event: The trusteeship ends for another reason, e.g. the trustee withdraws or the Minister redirects payment (the trustee must notify ESDC)

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: Social Security / SSI representative payee
jurisdictions.summary: A person or organization that the Social Security Administration (SSA) selects to receive Social Security (Title II) or SSI (Title XVI) benefits for a beneficiary. SSA appoints a payee after finding that the beneficiary cannot manage or direct the management of their benefit payments. In this role, 'incapacitated' means that SSA administrative finding. It is not a court adjudication, and SSA can appoint a payee even for a legally competent person. A payee is not an agent: a power of attorney, including a durable one, gives no authority to receive or negotiate these benefits. The appointment ends when SSA changes payees, when SSA finds the beneficiary capable, or when the beneficiary dies. The former payee must then return payments not due and hand over conserved funds.

assigned.event: SSA determines representative payment is in the beneficiary's interest, then selects a payee using its order of preference, with advance designees considered first

starts.event: SSA certifies payment to the payee after written advance notice. If the beneficiary protests or appeals within 10 days of a mailed notice, the action is delayed.

ends.event: Beneficiary dies: Title II entitlement ends with the month before death, and SSI payments stop after the month of death. The payee must return payments not due. Conserved funds belong to the estate.
SSA makes a new capability determination that the beneficiary is capable, and pays the beneficiary directly
SSA stops paying this payee and selects a new payee (misuse, payee's death, unwillingness, inability, failure to account or cooperate)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Centrelink payment nominee
jurisdictions.summary: A person or organisation appointed in writing by the Secretary (through Services Australia) to receive some or all of a person's Centrelink payments. Payment to the nominee counts as payment to the person. The appointment needs the nominee's written consent and must take the person's wishes into account. It does not depend on the person lacking capacity.

assigned.event: Secretary appoints the nominee in writing and directs that all or part of a payment go to the nominee. The nominee must consent in writing, and the principal's wishes must be considered. In practice the principal and nominee set it up jointly, online or by form.

starts.event: When the written appointment and payment direction are in force. A copy goes to both the nominee and the principal.

ends.event: Nominee tells the Secretary in writing they no longer wish to act. The Secretary must revoke as soon as practicable, effective from a later day named in the revocation.
Principal cancels the voluntary arrangement (myGov, phone or service centre)
Secretary revokes after the nominee reports a change in circumstances in response to a s 123K notice, or fails to comply with a s 123K/123L notice (e.g. a statement of how money was spent)

Death of the principal: the payment stops (final payment for allowees up to the day before death; pensioners are paid for the fortnight of death). After that, the executor or administrator deals with Services Australia. Part 3A has no express termination-on-death provision.

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Centrelink correspondence nominee
jurisdictions.summary: A person or organisation appointed by the Secretary to deal with Centrelink for a benefit recipient: making claims, receiving notices and meeting most requirements. The same person can be both payment and correspondence nominee. Suspension, revocation and the effect of death work the same way as for a payment nominee.

assigned.event: Secretary appoints the nominee in writing, with the nominee's written consent and after considering the principal's wishes

starts.event: On appointment. From then on the nominee may do any act the benefit recipient may do under social security law (except Part 3A matters, and acts a notice requires the recipient to do personally), and notices may be given to the nominee.

ends.event: Nominee withdraws in writing (mandatory revocation), or Secretary revokes for change of circumstances or non-compliance
Principal cancels the voluntary arrangement
Death of the principal: there is no longer a benefit recipient to act for, and Services Australia deals with the executor or administrator. No express statutory termination.

jurisdictions.summary: Protection of an adult runs through the Code Civil, but the Mental Health Care Act supplies a distinctly Mauritian trigger: where a review finds a patient likely to stay over six months with significant assets to protect, the Ministère Public applies to the Judge in Chambers for an ouverture de tutelle.

assigned.event: An adult whose altered faculties leave them unable to look after their own interests is protected by law, the alteration being medically established

starts.event: Judge in Chambers orders the ouverture de tutelle and appoints a tuteur; under the Mental Health Care Act this follows a report that the patient will stay over six months and has significant assets

ends.event: Death of the protected person; the estate passes to the heirs by saisine

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator (letters of curatorship)
jurisdictions.summary: South Africa’s statutory substitute decision maker for property. Nobody may administer another’s property as curator without letters of curatorship from the Master, and the letters themselves fix the authority — a single act, care of the property, full administration, or carrying on a business.

assigned.event: Curator nominated by will or written instrument, or the Master appoints one where there is no nomination, where an absentee owns property, or where a court could appoint

starts.event: On letters of curatorship being granted by the Master; without them no one may take care of or administer the property

ends.event: Removal from office, the removal provisions for executors applying to curators
Death of the person, when the estate passes to the executor

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator of property (Mental Health Care Act)
jurisdictions.summary: The modern route for property, running alongside curatorship under the Administration of Estates Act. A Master of a High Court appoints an administrator to care for and administer the property of a mentally ill person or a person with severe or profound intellectual disability.

assigned.event: Any person over 18 applies in writing, under oath or solemn affirmation, to a Master of a High Court, or a High Court orders an appointment after an appeal or enquiry

starts.event: The Master appoints an administrator to care for and administer the property

ends.event: Term of office terminated on application by the person concerned, the administrator, or whoever applied for the appointment
Death of the person, when the estate passes to the executor

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Custodian of a missing person’s property (财产代管人)

nameEn.en: Custodian of a missing person’s property

jurisdictions.summary: Two years after a person drops out of contact, an interested party may apply to have them declared missing; their property is then held by spouse, adult children, parents or another willing person, or by someone the court designates where that is disputed or nobody is able. The custodian pays the missing person’s taxes and debts out of the property and answers for loss caused intentionally or by gross negligence.

assigned.event: An interested party applies to the People’s Court to declare the person missing, two years after they were last heard of

starts.event: The property is held by spouse, adult children, parents or another willing person; where that is disputed, nobody qualifies, or they are unable, by a person the court designates

ends.event: An interested party, or the custodian with good reason, applies to the court to change the custodian, who must hand over the property and report
The missing person reappears, the court revokes the declaration, and the property is handed back on demand
The person is declared dead, and succession opens

jurisdictions.label: Japan
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator (保佐人)
jurisdictions.summary: The middle tier, for a person whose capacity to appreciate their situation is markedly insufficient. It is expressly unavailable where the heavier ground for guardianship applies, so the tiers do not overlap.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates the commencement of curatorship where capacity is markedly insufficient, except where the ground for guardianship applies

starts.event: On the adjudication of commencement of curatorship

ends.event: Death of the person, which commences the inheritance

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Deputy for property and affairs
jurisdictions.summary: Where P lacks capacity the court may either make the decision itself or appoint a deputy to make it. A deputy over property and affairs must be 21 or over and act without remuneration, unless they are a professional deputy unrelated to P.

assigned.event: Court finds P lacks capacity in relation to property and affairs and appoints a deputy rather than deciding the matter itself

starts.event: On appointment, within the powers the order confers

ends.event: Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Limited guardian
jurisdictions.summary: A lighter court regime: the ward keeps capacity except for acts the court lists as needing the limited guardian’s consent. Representation is not automatic — the court must confer it separately.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of limited guardianship

starts.event: Court determines the scope of acts requiring the limited guardian’s consent; the court may separately confer a right of representation

ends.event: Guardianship contract supervisor appointed, or adult guardianship adjudged, displacing the limited guardianship
Death of the ward

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Værge

citation.title: Guardianship – The Agency of Family Law
citation.quote: Persons to be placed under guardianship cannot choose their own guardian, but their wishes are taken into account.

jurisdictions.summary: Guardianship may be established for an adult who, through mental illness including severe dementia, impaired development or other seriously weakened health, cannot manage their own affairs, and only where there is a need.

assigned.event: Værgemål established for an adult unable to manage their affairs

starts.event: On the order

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Edunvalvoja

citation.cite: Guardianship Service Act 442/1999 s 4 (amendments up to 637/2022)
citation.title: Guardianship Service Act (unofficial translation published on Finlex)
citation.quote: The guardian of an adult is the person who a court or the guardianship authority has appointed as the adult's guardian.

jurisdictions.summary: A court may appoint a guardian for an adult who cannot look after their interests and whose affairs are not being handled adequately in any other way.

assigned.event: Court appoints where the adult cannot safeguard their interests

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Curateur
jurisdictions.summary: Assistance rather than representation, for someone not incapable of acting but needing continuous help with important civil acts. Expressly subsidiary: curatelle is pronounced only if sauvegarde de justice would not suffice.

assigned.event: Application to the juge des tutelles for a person whose faculties are medically established as impaired

starts.event: Court places the person under curatelle, having found that sauvegarde de justice cannot give sufficient protection

ends.event: Measure lifted or replaced by tutelle
Death; the heirs are seised of right

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Tuteur
jurisdictions.summary: Continuous representation in civil acts, and the last rung of the ladder: tutelle is pronounced only where neither sauvegarde de justice nor curatelle would give sufficient protection.

assigned.event: Application to the juge des tutelles where the person must be represented continuously in civil acts

starts.event: Court places the person under tutelle, having found neither sauvegarde de justice nor curatelle sufficient

ends.event: Measure lifted or lightened to curatelle
Death; the heirs are seised of right

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Rechtlicher Betreuer (Vermögenssorge)
jurisdictions.summary: The same court appointment where the assigned remit covers property and financial affairs.

assigned.event: Betreuungsgericht assigns a remit covering property affairs

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Decision-making representative (property and affairs)
jurisdictions.summary: The same court-appointed office as for personal welfare, where the order covers property and affairs instead of or as well as welfare.

assigned.event: Court declares the person lacks capacity and no suitable or registered co-decision-maker exists

starts.event: Court order appointing a decision-making representative for specified property and affairs decisions

ends.event: Court varies or discharges the order
Death of the relevant person; the estate vests in the personal representatives

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator of a person declared incapable (curatore dell’inabilitato)

nameEn.en: Curator of a person declared incapable

jurisdictions.summary: The middle measure, for an adult of unsound mind whose state is not grave enough for interdiction. The rules on curatorship of emancipated minors apply, so the person acts but needs the curator’s assistance for acts beyond ordinary administration.

assigned.event: An adult of unsound mind whose condition is not grave enough for interdiction may be declared incapable

starts.event: The provisions on curatorship of emancipated minors apply to the curatorship of the person declared incapable

ends.event: The measure is revoked, or replaced by support administration where its conditions are met

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Curator
jurisdictions.summary: The heaviest of the three court measures, reaching both person and property, and expressly subsidiary: the kantonrechter may not impose it where a more appropriate and less far-reaching measure would do.

assigned.event: Interested party applies to the kantonrechter for ondercuratelestelling

starts.event: Kantonrechter places the adult under curatele, on finding they cannot properly look after their interests or endanger their own or others' safety, and that no more appropriate, less far-reaching measure suffices

ends.event: Curatele lifted by the kantonrechter
Death; the heirs succeed of right

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Bewindvoerder
jurisdictions.summary: Property only, and it can be placed over particular goods rather than the whole estate, for a fixed or open-ended period. The person keeps every non-property decision.

assigned.event: Application to the kantonrechter for bewind over one or more of the adult's goods

starts.event: Kantonrechter institutes bewind over specified goods, for a fixed or indefinite term, where the adult cannot fully look after their property interests

ends.event: Bewind terminated by the kantonrechter or on expiry of its term
Death; the estate passes to the heirs of right

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Curador
jurisdictions.summary: A court establishes curatela only where no other support measure suffices, and specifies the acts for which assistance is required. Representative curatela is exceptional.

assigned.event: Judicial authority constitutes curatela by reasoned decision

starts.event: On the judicial resolution

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: Förvaltare

citation.cite: Government Offices of Sweden, Administrators, guardians ad litem and continuing powers of attorney (published 8 April 2025)
citation.title: Administrators
citation.quote: If a person cannot take care of themself, a court may appoint an administrator (förvaltare) for them.

jurisdictions.summary: The stronger measure, available only where the person is unable to care for themselves or their property and godmanskap is not enough.

assigned.event: Court orders förvaltarskap

starts.event: On the court's decision

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Property and financial affairs deputy
jurisdictions.summary: The Court of Protection appoints a deputy, by order, to make property and financial decisions for a person (P) who lacks capacity for those matters. The appointment lasts until the court discharges it, P regains capacity, or P dies.

assigned.event: Court of Protection order under MCA s 16

starts.event: When the court order is issued (for property deputies, after any required security bond is in place)

ends.event: P dies: the deputyship ends (deputy tells OPG and the court; the final report may be required)
P regains capacity: the deputy loses power over matters P can decide, and the order is discharged on application (form COP9)
Court revokes the appointment or varies/discharges the order (e.g. deputy acting outside authority or not in P's best interests), or order expires
Deputy steps down (court order needed) or dies (sole/joint deputyship ends)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Controller appointed by the High Court (Office of Care and Protection)
jurisdictions.summary: When the High Court is satisfied on medical evidence that a person is incapable, by reason of mental disorder, of managing their property and affairs, it may appoint a controller to act as it orders or authorises. Proceedings run through the Office of Care and Protection. A controller is discharged automatically on the patient's death.

assigned.event: High Court order appointing controller (interim powers possible pending determination)

starts.event: On the order, within the powers the court confers

ends.event: Death of the patient: discharged without any order
Court satisfied the patient has become capable: discharged by order
Court discharges at any time if expedient

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Guardian with powers over property and financial affairs
jurisdictions.summary: A guardian appointed by the sheriff to manage the adult's property or financial affairs, or specified parts of them. Supervised by the Public Guardian (Scotland).

assigned.event: Sheriff grants a guardianship order on application (adult incapable and likely to remain so; no other AWI measure sufficient)

starts.event: On the order. The Public Guardian registers the appointment and issues a certificate of appointment (after caution/security is found, if required).

ends.event: Order expires at the end of its period (3 years by default, or another period including indefinite) unless renewed. It continues while a renewal application is pending.
Sheriff recalls the order, or replaces/removes the guardian
Public Guardian (financial powers) or local authority/Mental Welfare Commission (welfare powers) recalls the powers
Guardian resigns
Death of the adult: the guardianship order ceases to have effect

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Committee of the estate (Patients Property Act)
localNames: Public Guardian and Trustee as committee
jurisdictions.summary: A court-appointed committee for an adult declared incapable of managing their affairs. The committee has all the adult's rights and powers over the estate, except making a will. It must account to the Public Guardian and Trustee. After the patient's death, and until a representation grant is issued and served on it, the committee keeps its powers and also has a personal representative's powers.

assigned.event: Court declares adult incapable of managing affairs and appoints committee (or PGT by default)

starts.event: On the court order; any power of attorney terminates

ends.event: Court declares the person no longer incapable, then discharges the committee after accounts are passed
After death: when a representation grant has issued and written notice of it has been served on the committee (committee then accounts to the executor or administrator and may be discharged)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Statutory property guardian (Public Guardian and Trustee by certificate of incapability)
jurisdictions.summary: An administrative route without a court. A qualified health care provider assesses the adult and reports to a health authority designate, who may issue a certificate of incapability after consulting the Public Guardian and Trustee (PGT) and notifying the adult and family. The PGT then becomes statutory property guardian. That suspends powers of attorney, which terminate if the PGT decides to manage the property.

assigned.event: Health authority designate issues a certificate of incapability

starts.event: As of the date the certificate is signed

ends.event: PGT satisfied the adult no longer needs a guardian and gives notice
Reassessment finds capability, accepted by health authority designate
Court ends it on review, or appoints a Patients Property Act committee
Adult dies: committee powers continue until a representation grant is served

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Statutory guardian of property (Public Guardian and Trustee)
jurisdictions.summary: The PGT becomes statutory guardian of property without a court order in two cases: when a Mental Health Act certificate finds a psychiatric-facility patient incapable of managing property, or when a capacity assessor issues a certificate of incapacity after a s 16 request (the requester must have found no attorney with authority over all property and no family member planning to apply to court). A qualifying family member may later replace the PGT (s 17).

assigned.event: MHA certificate of incapacity to manage property (s 15) or assessor's certificate of incapacity (s 16)

starts.event: s 15: when the MHA certificate is issued. s 16: as soon as the PGT receives its copy of the assessor's certificate.

ends.event: The person dies
Court appoints a guardian of property under s 22
Attorney under a pre-existing CPOA over all property gives the PGT the POA, an undertaking and proof of identity
Capacity restored: MHA certificate cancelled or patient discharged (s 15 cases), an assessor's notice of capacity, or a final Consent and Capacity Board or court finding of capacity
Guardian resigns with notice

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Court-appointed guardian of property
jurisdictions.summary: On any person's application, the Superior Court may appoint a guardian of property for someone incapable of managing property who needs decisions made. It will not do so if a less restrictive alternative that needs no incapacity finding would meet the need. Paid care or service providers are ineligible unless they are a spouse, partner, relative or attorney. The PGT is appointed only with its consent and as a last resort.

assigned.event: Court order under s 22 (Part III procedure)

starts.event: On the court's appointment

ends.event: Court terminates the guardianship on motion (e.g. capacity regained)
The incapable person dies. The estate passes to the personal representative, and the guardian must pass accounts on request.
ends.note: No express 'death terminates court guardianship of property' text was found in the SDA. The end follows from EAA s 2 vesting property in the personal representative.

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Temporary representative of an incapable person of full age
jurisdictions.summary: Created by S.Q. 2020, c. 11 (in force 1 November 2022) to avoid a full tutorship. The court, after medical and psychosocial assessments, authorizes a person to perform one specific act for an incapable adult, such as selling a property. The authority ends when that act is done, or on the institution of tutorship or homologation of a protection mandate.

assigned.event: Court authorization on application by the spouse, relatives, an interested person, mandatary, Public Curator, or the person

starts.event: On the judgment, on terms fixed by the court

ends.event: Specific act performed; representative notifies the person and the Public Curator
Tutorship instituted or protection mandate homologated

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Tutor to property of a person of full age
jurisdictions.summary: The court may appoint a tutor to property to administer an incapable adult's patrimony, separately from or together with a tutor to the person. Tutorship also completes a protection mandate that does not fully cover administration. It ends on a judgment of release or the adult's death, after which the liquidator takes seisin.

assigned.event: Court institutes tutorship to property

starts.event: On the judgment

ends.event: Judgment of release or unopposed cessation report
Death of the person; liquidator exercises seisin from the opening of the succession

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Close relative exercising a deceased person’s information rights (近亲属)

nameEn.en: Close relative exercising a deceased person’s information rights

jurisdictions.summary: The Personal Information Protection Law is where China answers the digital-estate question. On a natural person’s death their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise the rights of that chapter — access, copy, correct, delete — over the deceased’s personal information, except where the deceased arranged otherwise before death. The Civil Code adds only that data and online virtual property are protected as other law provides.

assigned.event: The person dies, leaving personal information held by handlers; the Civil Code protects data and online virtual property as other law provides

starts.event: Close relatives may exercise the rights of access, copying, correction and deletion, for their own lawful and legitimate interests

ends.event: The deceased arranged otherwise before death, which displaces the relatives’ exercise of those rights

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Héritier exerçant les droits sur les données
jurisdictions.summary: Absent directives, heirs may exercise the data-protection rights themselves, but only so far as settling the succession and having the death taken into account require — including receiving digital goods or data resembling family mementos, and closing the deceased's accounts.

assigned.event: Heirship, where the deceased left no directives or the directives do not provide otherwise

starts.event: On death, to the extent necessary to organise and settle the succession — accessing processing to identify information useful to liquidation and partition, and receiving digital goods or data resembling family mementos — and to have the death taken into account

ends.event: Accounts closed, processing objected to or updated; the controller must show, free of charge, that it complied
Disagreement between heirs, referred to the tribunal judiciaire

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Person exercising a deceased person’s data rights (diritti riguardanti le persone decedute)

nameEn.en: Person exercising a deceased person’s data rights

jurisdictions.summary: Italy’s answer to the digital estate, and among the most explicit anywhere. The GDPR rights of access through to objection may be exercised over a deceased person’s data by someone with an interest of their own, by their mandatary acting to protect them, or for family reasons deserving protection. But the person may forbid it — and the prohibition binds only as against directly offered information society services, must be unequivocal, specific, free and informed, may cover only some of the rights, is revocable at any time, and can never prejudice third parties’ property rights arising from the death or the defence of one’s interests in court.

assigned.event: The person dies, leaving personal data held by controllers

starts.event: Someone with an interest of their own, a mandatary acting to protect the data subject, or a person acting for family reasons deserving protection exercises the rights in GDPR arts 15 to 22

ends.event: The person expressly forbade it in writing to the controller, limited to the direct offer of information society services
The prohibition is revoked or modified, which the person may do at any time

jurisdictions.roleName: Fiduciary seeking access to digital assets (PR, conservator, agent, trustee)
jurisdictions.summary: RUFADAA gives no new fiduciary status of its own. It sets out when an existing personal representative, conservator, agent, or trustee can get a digital-asset catalogue or content from a custodian. By default, content of electronic communications needs the user's consent (or, for a personal representative, a court direction). A conservator also needs a court order after a chance for a hearing.

assigned.event: Underlying fiduciary status arises under other law (POA, trust, court appointment, letters or small-estate affidavit)

starts.event: Written request with required documents; custodian must comply within [60] days

ends.event: Underlying authority ends (e.g., agent's POA ends at principal's death, conservatorship ends, PR appointment terminates)
Estate closed

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Personal representative entitled to possession and disposal of the body
jurisdictions.summary: No one owns a dead body. At common law the duty to arrange proper disposal falls first on the personal representatives. An executor can claim possession of the body even before probate. An administrator has the same duty but may not be able to get an injunction for the body before the grant. For cremation, an executor or a near relative aged 16+ applies. If no suitable arrangements are made, the local authority must bury or cremate the body.

assigned.event: By law on death: executor named in will; otherwise those entitled to administer

starts.event: At death (executor, before probate); administrator's enforceable right may await the grant

ends.event: Body buried or cremated
High Court passes over the executor (SCA 1981 s 116 limited grant) or the local authority acts under PH(CD)A 1984 s 46

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor or nearest surviving relative (disposal of remains)
jurisdictions.summary: NI has no statutory priority list for who controls disposal of a body. Cremation in Belfast requires an application by the executor or nearest surviving relative, or a satisfactory explanation why someone else is applying. Cremation is unlawful if the deceased left a written direction against it. Whoever arranges the funeral is responsible for the bill.

assigned.event: Executor named in will, or nearest surviving relative at death

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Burial or cremation completed (ashes notice to applicant/relative/executor)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Person entitled to arrange burial, cremation or hydrolysis
jurisdictions.summary: If an adult made an 'arrangements on death declaration', the person it names makes the arrangements. Otherwise, or if that is impracticable, the nearest relative under a statutory list may do so. The list runs: spouse or civil partner, cohabitant of 6 months or more, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, uncle or aunt, cousin, niece or nephew, then friend of long standing. The executor is not on the list.

assigned.event: Adult makes an arrangements on death declaration, or statute ranks the nearest relative immediately before death

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Remains buried, cremated or hydrolysed

localNames: person with the right to control the disposition
personal representative named in the will
jurisdictions.summary: The right to control disposition of human remains passes in this order: the personal representative named in the will, spouse, adult child, adult grandchild, guardian (for a minor), parent, adult sibling, adult nephew or niece, adult next of kin, the ministry or PGT, then another adult with a personal relationship. Written preferences in a will or preneed contract bind that person unless unreasonable. Funeral providers need that person's written authorization.

assigned.event: Will names a personal representative, or by statutory order at death

starts.event: At death

ends.event: Remains disposed of
Person unavailable or unwilling: right passes to next in priority
Supreme Court orders sole right to another applicant

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Estate trustee's right and duty to dispose of the body
jurisdictions.summary: No Ontario statute sets a priority list for who controls disposal of remains. Under case law (Saleh v Reichert, 1993), the estate trustee has the duty and authority to dispose of the body and may follow the deceased's lawful wishes. The funeral regulations assume a 'purchaser' and a 'personal representative' but do not rank decision-makers. Cremation also needs a coroner's certificate.

assigned.event: Person named executor in will, or person entitled to be administrator

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Remains disposed of (burial, cremation or other lawful means)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Heirs or successors deciding funeral arrangements and disposal of the body
jurisdictions.summary: A person of full age may decide the nature of their funeral and the disposal of their body. Without expressed wishes, the wishes of the heirs or successors prevail. Either way, the heirs or successors must act, and the costs are charged to the succession. No one may embalm, bury or cremate a body before an attestation of death and a 6-hour wait.

assigned.event: By law at death: heirs or successors (implementing the deceased's wishes if expressed)

starts.event: At death; disposal no earlier than 6 hours after attestation of death

ends.event: Funeral and disposal carried out (expenses charged to the succession)

starts.event: Death of decedent

ends.event: Right relinquished to the next class if the holder fails to act or delegate within 7 days (10 days for a surviving spouse) or cannot be found

ends.note: No explicit statutory end point; inferred from the nature of the right.

jurisdictions.summary: The person with legal authority to authorize and direct disposition of a decedent's remains, including cremation, under Florida's funeral and cemetery law.

assigned.event: Priority: (1) decedent's own written inter vivos authorization; (2) DD Form 93 designee if decedent died in military service; (3) surviving spouse; (4) adult child; (5) parent; (6) adult sibling; (7) adult grandchild; (8) grandparent; (9) next degree of kinship; if none, fallback includes guardian at death, PR, attorney in fact at death, health surrogate at death, public officials, institution, or a willing friend

starts.event: Death of the decedent

ends.event: Cremated remains unclaimed 90 days after cremation: establishment may dispose
Final disposition completed (statute does not state an explicit end point)

jurisdictions.roleName: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: agent to control disposition of remains
jurisdictions.summary: The person who holds the right to control disposition of a decedent's remains, including cremation, and who is liable for reasonable disposition costs under the Illinois Disposition of Remains Act.

assigned.event: Decedent may appoint an agent in a notarized statutory-form instrument (or in a will, prepaid funeral contract, health care POA with disposition power, or cremation authorization form); otherwise priority: designated agent; executor acting on will instructions; spouse; adult child(ren) (majority); parents; next of kin (majority); religious/civic organization; public official for indigents; institution; any other person assuming responsibility

starts.event: Decedent's death (form: 'This appointment becomes effective upon my death'); agent's authority is not effective until agent signs acceptance

ends.event: Right relinquished if charged with first or second degree murder or voluntary manslaughter in connection with the death
Disposition carried out (end point not stated in statute)

jurisdictions.label: US — Louisiana
jurisdictions.roleName: Person with the right to control interment

assigned.event: Designated by the decedent in a notarial testament or a written and notarized declaration; otherwise by the statutory priority

starts.event: Death of the decedent

jurisdictions.label: US — Maine
jurisdictions.roleName: Person with custody and control of remains
localNames: written and signed document designating a person
jurisdictions.summary: A person may name who will have custody and control of their remains in a written, signed document; absent that, a ranked next-of-kin list applies, and the right lapses if it is not exercised within 4 days of death.

assigned.event: Subject designates a person in a written and signed document

starts.event: On death, custody and control vest in the designated person, or in the next of kin if none was designated or the designee refuses

ends.event: Final disposition carried out
Right not exercised within 4 days of death, so it passes to the next lower level of priority
Holder charged with murder or manslaughter forfeits the right, regaining it in the same priority if the charges are dismissed or the person is acquitted before final disposition

jurisdictions.label: US — Michigan
jurisdictions.roleName: Funeral representative

assigned.event: Designated in writing by an individual 18 or older of sound mind, ahead of the statutory family priority

starts.event: Death of the decedent; the designee is presumed to hold the right and power over funeral arrangements and disposition

jurisdictions.label: US — New Jersey
jurisdictions.roleName: Person appointed to control the funeral and disposition

assigned.event: Appointed in the will, or since 2019 in a separate writing before two witnesses on a board-approved form

starts.event: Death; the appointee may act before the will is probated

jurisdictions.label: US — New York
jurisdictions.roleName: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: person designated in a written instrument under PHL §4201
jurisdictions.summary: The person who has the right to control disposition of remains and must carry out the decedent's directions where lawful and practicable.

assigned.event: Decedent signs statutory written instrument before two adult witnesses

starts.event: Death ('becomes effective upon my death')

ends.event: Agent not reasonably available, unwilling or not competent: next class assumes control
Disposition completed
ends.note: No explicit statutory end point or day-count forfeiture found in retrieved text.

jurisdictions.label: US — North Carolina
jurisdictions.roleName: Person authorised to dispose of the body
jurisdictions.summary: An adult may direct the type, place and method of disposition of their own body, through a ranked list of instruments beginning with a preneed funeral contract and a health care power of attorney.

assigned.event: Individual aged 18 or over authorises disposition by one of the ranked methods

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Disposition carried out

jurisdictions.label: US — Ohio
jurisdictions.roleName: Representative assigned the right of disposition
jurisdictions.summary: An adult may assign the right to control disposition of their own body to a named representative, or a group acting collectively, by a written declaration.

assigned.event: Declarant executes a written declaration appointing a representative

starts.event: On the declarant's death

ends.event: Disposition carried out

jurisdictions.label: US — Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.roleName: Person with the right to dispose of a decedent's remains

assigned.event: Surviving spouse by operation of §305, subject to the decedent's will and any waiver and agreement

ends.event: Authority defeated by enduring estrangement, incompetence, contrary intent, or waiver and agreement, proven by clear and convincing evidence

jurisdictions.label: US — Texas
jurisdictions.roleName: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: agent under Appointment for Disposition of Remains
jurisdictions.summary: The person who controls disposition of remains, including cremation, and must inter them. That person is liable for the reasonable cost of interment (except an executor or administrator) and may seek reimbursement from the estate.

assigned.event: Decedent signs a written instrument (statutory form available) with acknowledged signature naming agent and successors

starts.event: Decedent's death; agent must sign acceptance before acting

ends.event: Holder fails to make or delegate arrangements by the earlier of the 6th day after notice of death or the 10th day after death; right passes
Remains interred / disposition completed
ends.note: No explicit statutory end point; inferred.

jurisdictions.label: US — Washington
jurisdictions.roleName: Person controlling disposition of remains
localNames: written document expressing the decedent's wishes
jurisdictions.summary: A person controls the disposition of their own remains, and a signed, witnessed written document stating their wishes is by itself sufficient authority to carry them out.

assigned.event: Person signs a written document stating their wishes, in the presence of a witness

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Disposition carried out

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Person entitled to arrange disposal of the body
jurisdictions.summary: No NSW statute sets a general order of priority. At common law the executor (or the person with the highest right to administration) is said to control disposal (Smith v Tamworth City Council); this is not verified from a primary source here. For cremation, the Public Health Regulation 2022 lets an executor or a nearest surviving relative apply. A medical referee must refuse a permit if cremation would go against the deceased's written direction.

assigned.event: Named executor in will; otherwise nearest surviving relative (for cremation application)

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Body buried or cremated

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Queensland
jurisdictions.roleName: Personal representative / close relative controlling disposal of remains
jurisdictions.summary: At common law the executor, or the person entitled to administration, has the right to custody of the body for burial. The Cremations Act 2003 lets a close relative or personal representative apply for permission to cremate. It qualifies the common-law right in three ways. The personal representative must carry out signed cremation instructions. Otherwise an objection by a spouse, adult child, parent or personal representative blocks cremation. The crematorium must follow the applicant's reasonable written instructions for the ashes.

assigned.event: Executor named in will; otherwise person entitled to administration (common law)

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Body buried, or cremated and ashes disposed of per applicant's instructions (or buried by crematorium after 1 year without instructions)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Person entitled to arrange disposal of remains (executor at common law; applicant for interment or cremation authorisation)
jurisdictions.summary: No Victorian statute says who controls disposal of a body. The Cemeteries and Crematoria Act 2003 lets 'a person who wishes' remains to be interred or cremated apply to the cemetery trust. The trust may require consent from the holder of the right of interment. At common law the executor, or where none the person with the best claim to administration, has the right to possession of the body for disposal.

assigned.event: Executor named in will (common law); otherwise the person entitled to administration

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Body buried or cremated

jurisdictions.label: Argentina
jurisdictions.roleName: Persona con derecho a decidir las exequias

nameEn.en: Person entitled to decide the funeral

jurisdictions.summary: A fully capable person may direct the manner and circumstances of their funeral and burial in any form. If no wish was expressed or can be presumed, the decision falls to the spouse, then the cohabitant, and failing them the relatives.

assigned.event: The person directs the manner and circumstances of their exequias in any form; otherwise the statutory order applies

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Funeral and burial carried out
