jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Donor of body or tissue, or the family in the statutory order
localNames: donation of human bodies and tissue
jurisdictions.summary: A person competent to make a will may donate their body or specified tissue by will, by a document signed before two competent witnesses, or by an oral statement before two. The donation must name a donee or it is null and void. Absent a donation or a contrary direction, the family may donate in a fixed order.

assigned.event: Person competent to make a will donates the body or specified tissue by will, signed document before two witnesses, or oral statement before two witnesses

starts.event: After the person’s death; the donation must have nominated a donee or it is null and void

ends.event: Donation acted on, or the family donate in the statutory order where the deceased made none

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Donation decision maker (人体器官捐献决定人)
jurisdictions.summary: A citizen with full capacity decides for themselves, in writing or by will, and may revoke a willingness already expressed. An objection expressed before death is absolute: no organisation or individual may then donate or procure. Only where the person expressed no objection may spouse, adult children and parents jointly decide, in writing, after death.

assigned.event: A person with full capacity decides to donate, in writing or by will; nobody may coerce, deceive or induce them

starts.event: Procurement takes place only after death has been determined as the law requires, and the staff who procure or transplant may not take part in determining death

ends.event: The person revokes a willingness to donate already expressed
The person expressed an objection before death, after which no organisation or individual may donate or procure

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Person authorising removal of organs
localNames: person lawfully in possession of the dead body
jurisdictions.summary: A donor may authorise removal in writing before two or more witnesses, at least one a near relative. Failing that, if the person expressed no objection in life, the person lawfully in possession of the body may authorise removal unless a near relative objects.

assigned.event: Donor unequivocally authorises removal in writing before two or more witnesses, at least one of whom is a near relative

starts.event: After death, the person lawfully in possession of the body must give reasonable facilities for removal, unless they believe the authority was revoked

ends.event: Removal carried out, or a near relative objects where the deceased left no authority

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Designated officer authorising organ removal, subject to a registered objection
jurisdictions.summary: Singapore presumes consent. A hospital’s designated officer may authorise removal of an organ from a person who died there, and the block is not a missing consent but a registered objection: no authority may be given where the deceased registered an objection with the Director-General during their lifetime. An objection may be withdrawn at any time.

assigned.event: A person may register an objection to removal of an organ with the Director-General, in the prescribed form, or leave the register untouched

starts.event: On death in hospital the designated officer may authorise removal in writing, unless the deceased had registered an objection

ends.event: Removal authorised and carried out, or barred by a registered objection

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Afdødes egen bestemmelse om vævsudtagelse

nameEn.en: The deceased's own decision on tissue removal

jurisdictions.summary: Denmark requires the donor's own decision: tissue may be taken where the deceased, after turning 18, decided so in writing, and relatives cannot override a written decision.

assigned.event: The deceased's own written determination made after turning 18

starts.event: After death at a hospital or similar institution

ends.event: Procedure carried out or refused

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Vainajan tahto elinluovutuksessa

nameEn.en: Wishes of the deceased in organ donation

jurisdictions.summary: Finland presumes consent: organs may be removed unless it is known, or there is reason to assume, that the deceased would have opposed it. An express prohibition in life is binding.

assigned.event: By law; the deceased's own position in life governs

starts.event: After death

ends.event: Removal carried out, or barred by the deceased's prohibition

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Proches et registre national des refus

nameEn.en: Relatives and the national refusal register

jurisdictions.summary: Presumed consent. Removal may be carried out on any adult who did not make their refusal known in life, principally by entry on the national register; the refusal is revocable at any time, and the doctor informs the relatives of the nature and purpose beforehand.

assigned.event: Person may record a refusal in life, principally by entry on the national automated register; the refusal is revocable at any time

starts.event: On death duly established: removal may proceed unless a refusal was made known, and the doctor first informs the relatives of its nature and purpose

ends.event: Removal carried out or abandoned; the Agence de la biomédecine is notified beforehand

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Nächster Angehöriger / benannte Person (Organspende)
jurisdictions.summary: Germany is opt-in. Absent the donor's own declaration the next of kin decides, bound by the donor's presumed wishes; the donor may instead nominate a specific person.

assigned.event: Statutory next-of-kin order, or a person the donor nominated

starts.event: After death is established and no declaration by the donor is found

ends.event: Decision given or refused

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Designated family member (organ donation)
jurisdictions.summary: Ireland moved to soft opt-out on 17 June 2025. Consent is deemed unless an objection is on the Register, but the family member is not bypassed: if none can be identified or confirmed, deemed consent does not apply at all.

assigned.event: Status arises by relationship at death; the person themselves may instead register an objection on the Opt-Out Register

starts.event: On death, where deemed consent does not apply — including where the deceased was not ordinarily resident for 12 months, lacked capacity to understand the deemed-consent scheme, is a child, or where no designated family member can be identified

ends.event: Consent given or withheld, and removal for transplantation carried out or not

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Organ donation decision (dichiarazione di volontà; opposizione dei familiari)
jurisdictions.summary: Italy legislated presumed consent and then deferred it. Article 4 makes a failure to declare count as assent, but article 28(2) makes article 4 effective only from the activation of the transplant information system under article 7. Until that date article 23 governs: removal is permitted unless the person explicitly refused, and the non-separated spouse, the cohabiting partner, failing them adult children, failing them parents or the legal representative may lodge written opposition during the death-observation period.

assigned.event: Under the transitional rule, removal is permitted from a person whose death has been ascertained unless they explicitly refused assent

starts.event: The non-separated spouse, the cohabiting partner, failing them adult children, failing them parents or the legal representative may lodge written opposition within the death-observation period

ends.event: Opposition is not admitted where the person’s own documents or deposited declarations show a contrary wish
Article 4’s regime, under which a failure to declare counts as assent, takes effect only from the activation of the transplant information system

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Nabestaande (orgaandonatie)
jurisdictions.summary: The Netherlands runs an active-registration opt-out: an adult who answers nothing is entered in the donorregister as having no objection six weeks after a reminder. The family decides only where the person expressly left the decision to them.

assigned.event: Person records consent or objection, or leaves the decision to their relatives; silence is registered as 'geen bezwaar' six weeks after a reminder

starts.event: On death, where the register records that the decision was left to the relatives: the spouse, registered partner or other life companion, failing whom the immediately reachable adult blood relatives

ends.event: Consent given or refused after the donorregister has been consulted

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Persona cuya oposición consta (donación de órganos)

nameEn.en: Person whose objection is on record (organ donation)

jurisdictions.summary: Spain presumes donation: organs may be removed from the deceased unless they had expressly recorded their opposition.

assigned.event: By law; no appointment. The deceased's own recorded opposition governs

starts.event: After death is verified

ends.event: Removal carried out or barred by recorded opposition

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: Närstående vid transplantation

nameEn.en: Close relative in connection with transplantation

jurisdictions.summary: Sweden presumes consent: material may be taken unless the deceased objected in writing or otherwise expressed themselves against it. Relatives must be informed before the procedure.

assigned.event: By law; the deceased's own position governs, relatives are informed

starts.event: After death

ends.event: Procedure carried out or barred by the deceased's objection

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Nominated / appointed representative for organ and tissue consent
jurisdictions.summary: An adult can appoint one or more people to decide about consent after death, orally before two witnesses or in writing (witnessed, or in a will). This comes second: the deceased's own decision in force at death comes first. If no representative can act, England uses deemed consent for transplantation and Wales uses its 2013 Act.

assigned.event: Adult appoints orally (two witnesses) or in writing (signed and witnessed, or in a will)

starts.event: On the appointer's death, if no decision by the deceased was in force

ends.event: Revoked by the appointer (same formalities) or renounced by the representative
Representative not able to act, or not reasonably practicable to contact in time: appointment disregarded
Consent given or refused

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Person in a qualifying relationship (consent or objection to donation)
localNames: relative or friend of long standing
jurisdictions.summary: If the deceased left no decision and no representative can act, a person in the highest-ranking qualifying relationship matters in two ways. For activities that are not deemed (e.g. research, or excepted adults), they give or refuse consent. For transplantation in England or Wales, consent is deemed, but they can provide information that the deceased would not have consented, which stops the deemed consent.

assigned.event: By statute at death: ranking under HTA 2004 s 27(4) / Wales 2013 Act s 19(3)

starts.event: On death, where neither the deceased's own decision nor a nominated representative applies

ends.event: Consent given/refused, or objection information provided, or person left out of account (unwilling, unable, or not contactable in time)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Nominated representative (Human Tissue Act 2004 s 4)
jurisdictions.summary: An adult may appoint one or more people to deal with consent to donation and other scheduled activities after their death. A nominated representative's consent takes priority over deemed consent and over family members.

assigned.event: Adult appoints orally before two witnesses, or in writing (witnessed, or in a will)

starts.event: On death, if the deceased left no decision of their own in force

ends.event: Consent given or refused, or representative not reasonably contactable in time (appointment disregarded)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Person in a qualifying relationship (deemed consent regime)
jurisdictions.summary: Since the NI deemed-consent regime took effect in 2023, an adult who made no decision and appointed no representative is deemed to consent to transplantation, unless they are an excepted adult. The highest-ranked qualifying relative can block this only by giving information that would lead a reasonable person to conclude the deceased would not have consented. For excepted adults and non-transplant activities, that relative's consent is required.

assigned.event: By statute at death: ranking spouse/civil partner/partner; parent/child; sibling; grandparent/grandchild; sibling's child; step-parent; half-sibling; friend of long standing

starts.event: At death, where no own decision or nominated representative applies

ends.event: Consent given/refused, or deemed consent proceeds or is rebutted

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Nearest relative (Human Tissue (Scotland) Act 2006)
jurisdictions.summary: Since 26 March 2021, a Scottish-resident adult who made no express authorisation or opt-out declaration is deemed to authorise transplantation. The nearest relative, ranked by statute, has no general veto. Their role is to give evidence of the adult's latest views, and to authorise directly in the excepted cases: non-residents, adults incapable of understanding deemed authorisation, excepted body parts, and non-transplant purposes.

assigned.event: By statute at the relevant time: highest-ranked available relative under s 50 (spouse/civil partner, cohabitant of 6+ months, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, uncle/aunt, cousin, niece/nephew, longstanding friend)

starts.event: At death (or the relevant time for pre-death procedures), where the case is not covered by the adult's own express authorisation, opt-out or deemed authorisation

ends.event: Authorisation given (cannot be withdrawn for s 6E), or body released for disposal

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Person consenting to post-mortem tissue gift (Human Tissue Gift Act)
localNames: person lawfully in possession of the body
jurisdictions.summary: BC uses opt-in consent. A person 19 or older can consent in writing, or orally before 2 witnesses during a last illness, and that consent binds after death. Without it, consent can come from, in order: spouse, adult child, parent, adult sibling, other adult next of kin, then the person lawfully in possession of the body. Nobody may consent if there is reason to believe the deceased would have objected.

assigned.event: No consent by the person; the first readily available person in the s 5 order is entitled

starts.event: On death, or when a medical practitioner believes death is imminent and the person cannot consent

ends.event: Tissue removed or the gift cannot be used (body then dealt with as if no consent)
Known objection by the deceased or a person of the same or closer relationship

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Person who may consent to post-mortem donation (Gift of Life Act)
localNames: person lawfully in possession of the body
jurisdictions.summary: Ontario uses opt-in. A person 16 or older may consent to donation after death in a signed writing, or orally before two witnesses during their last illness, and that consent is binding at death. If they gave no consent, or cannot give one because death is imminent, the next person in the ranked list may consent: spouse, then child, parent, sibling, other next of kin, then the person lawfully in possession of the body (not a hospital administrative head). They may not consent if they believe the person would have objected.

assigned.event: By statute, in rank order, where the person has not given (or cannot give) consent

starts.event: On death, or when a physician is of the opinion that the person is incapable of consenting because of injury or disease and death is imminent

ends.event: The body or parts are used or removed under the consent, or a known objection by the person or a closer or equal relative prevents acting on it

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Person consenting to post-mortem organ or tissue removal
localNames: personne qui pouvait consentir aux soins
jurisdictions.summary: Québec uses opt-in consent. A person of full age, or a minor 14 or over, may give organs or tissues, verbally before 2 witnesses or in writing, including through the RAMQ register or the notaries' register. The wishes must be followed unless there is a compelling reason not to. jurisdictions.summary: NSW is opt-in. If the deceased gave unrevoked written consent, a hospital designated officer may authorise removal on that basis. Otherwise, provided the deceased had not objected, the senior available next of kin may consent: spouse or de facto partner, then adult child, then parent, then adult sibling. No next of kin of the same or higher class may object.

assigned.event: By operation of law under the s 4 definition at death

starts.event: On death, where the deceased's own written consent is not established

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Queensland
jurisdictions.roleName: Senior available next of kin (tissue donation)
jurisdictions.summary: Queensland uses opt-in consent. The deceased's own signed written consent, if not revoked, authorises removal. Otherwise a hospital designated officer may authorise removal if the senior available next of kin consents and reasonable inquiries show no objection by the deceased. The order is spouse, then adult child, then parent, then adult sibling. An objection by any one person of equal rank prevents removal. Since 2025 amendments, next of kin may also consent before death to ante-mortem interventions after a decision to withdraw life-sustaining measures.

assigned.event: By statutory definition (no appointment)

starts.event: After death (or before death to ante-mortem intervention once withdrawal of life-sustaining measures has been decided)

ends.event: Decision made / tissue removed

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Senior available next of kin (tissue donation)

Otherwise the senior available next of kin may consent, unless the deceased objected. The order is spouse or domestic partner, then adult child, then parent, then adult sibling. Next of kin may also give consent while the person is unconscious before death.

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Guardian appointed in advance by the adult (意定监护人)

nameEn.en: Guardian appointed in advance by the adult

jurisdictions.summary: An adult with full capacity may agree in advance, in writing, with a close relative or another willing person or organisation that they will act as guardian if capacity is later lost or partly lost. This, not the mandate, is the Civil Code’s durable arrangement: the guardian both represents the person in juristic acts and protects their personal and property rights.

assigned.event: The adult, while holding full capacity for civil conduct, settles their own guardian in writing after consulting close relatives or another willing person or organisation

starts.event: The appointed guardian performs guardianship duties when the adult loses or partly loses capacity for civil conduct

ends.event: The ward acquires or recovers full capacity for civil conduct, and the guardianship relationship terminates
Death of the ward or of the guardian
The People’s Court revokes the guardian’s qualification on application, for serious harm, neglect or other serious infringement

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Agency coupled with an interest
jurisdictions.summary: The only Indian agency that survives the principal’s incapacity or death — and it does so to protect the agent, not the principal. Where the agent has an interest in the property that is the subject-matter, the agency cannot be terminated to the prejudice of that interest, and the Act’s own illustration says it survives insanity and death.

assigned.event: Authority is given to an agent who has an interest in the property forming the subject-matter of the agency

starts.event: On the grant of authority

ends.event: Express contract providing for termination, or the interest ceasing; it is not ended by the principal’s insanity or death

jurisdictions.label: Japan
jurisdictions.roleName: Voluntary guardian (任意後見人)
jurisdictions.summary: Japan’s advance instrument, and it is deliberately hard to bring into force. The contract must be made as a notarial deed in the prescribed form, be registered, and by its own required terms takes effect only from the moment the Family Court appoints a supervisor — which it does once the person’s capacity has become insufficient.

assigned.event: Principal makes a voluntary guardianship contract delegating care and property affairs and conferring authority to represent, by notarial deed in the form prescribed by Ministry of Justice ordinance

starts.event: Only when the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, the contract being registered and the person’s capacity insufficient through mental disability

ends.event: The contract terminates if, after a supervisor has been appointed, the person receives an adjudication commencing statutory guardianship, curatorship or assistance
Death of the principal, which commences the inheritance

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Donee of a lasting power of attorney (property and affairs)
jurisdictions.summary: Registration is constitutive, not administrative: the Act says a lasting power of attorney is not created unless the instrument is made and registered in accordance with the First Schedule. Authority then covers property and affairs, and operates when P no longer has capacity to decide.

assigned.event: P executes an instrument conferring authority over property and affairs on a donee who meets the statutory requirements

starts.event: The power is not created until the instrument is made and registered; the authority then operates when P no longer has capacity to make the decision

ends.event: P revokes the power at any time while having capacity to do so
Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Voluntary guardian under a guardianship contract
jurisdictions.summary: Korea’s advance instrument. It must be made as an authentic deed and registered, and — unusually — it has no effect at all until the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, which it does once the principal is found to lack capacity.

assigned.event: Principal enters a guardianship contract in an authentic deed, entrusting property management and personal matters and conferring a right of representation

starts.event: Only when the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, the contract being registered and the principal deemed to lack capacity to manage affairs

ends.event: Contract terminates when commencement of adult or limited guardianship is adjudged for the principal
Death of the principal

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Fremtidsfuldmægtig

nameEn.en: Attorney under a future power of attorney

jurisdictions.summary: A future power of attorney. Denmark gates it at both ends: it is only valid if created in the national register and acknowledged before a notary, and it has no effect until the authority puts it into force on request.

assigned.event: Person aged 18 and able to act sensibly creates a fremtidsfuldmagt

starts.event: Only when the authority puts it into force on a request by the grantor or the attorneys jointly

ends.event: Death of the grantor; the estate passes to the arvinger

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Edunvalvontavaltuutettu

nameEn.en: Attorney under a continuing power of attorney

citation.cite: Act on the Continuing Power of Attorney 648/2007 s 2 (amendments up to 1140/2019)
citation.title: Act on the Continuing Power of Attorney (unofficial translation published on Finlex)
citation.quote: By a continuing power of attorney, the granter may authorise an attorney to represent the granter in matters concerning his or her property

jurisdictions.summary: A continuing power of attorney. It does not operate on signature: the guardianship authority must confirm it on the attorney's application, supported by a medical certificate.

assigned.event: Principal grants the authorisation in a written instrument

starts.event: When the guardianship authority confirms it on the attorney's application

ends.event: Death of the principal opens the estate to the osakkaat

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandataire de protection future

nameEn.en: Attorney under a future protection mandate

jurisdictions.summary: France's advance mandate is dormant until a court registry activates it. The mandataire must file the mandate and a medical certificate from a court-listed doctor at the tribunal judiciaire, and the clerk stamps it and dates its taking effect.

assigned.event: Any adult or emancipated minor not under tutelle or habilitation familiale mandates one or more people to represent them should they become unable to see to their own interests; a person under curatelle needs the curateur's assistance

starts.event: When it is established that the mandant can no longer see to their own interests: the mandataire produces the mandate and a certificate from a doctor on the art. 431 list to the registry of the tribunal judiciaire, and the greffier visas the mandate and dates its taking effect

ends.event: Death of the mandant; the heirs are seised of right
Revocation, or a judicial protection measure replacing the mandate

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Bevollmächtigter unter Vorsorgevollmacht (Vermögenssorge)

nameEn.en: Authorised person under a lasting power of attorney (care of assets)

jurisdictions.summary: An agent appointed by a private power of attorney. German authority is granted by unilateral declaration and, in doubt, survives both incapacity and the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal declares the power of attorney to the agent or to the third party

starts.event: On grant; the internal relationship may condition when it is used

ends.event: Revocation by the principal
Expiry of the underlying relationship; in doubt a mandate does NOT end on death or incapacity

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power (property and affairs)
jurisdictions.summary: Ireland's enduring power is dormant until two things both happen: the instrument is registered with the Decision Support Service and the donor actually lacks capacity. It confers no authority while the donor is capable.

assigned.event: Donor aged 18+ executes an instrument conferring general or specified authority over property and affairs

starts.event: Only once the instrument is registered under s 69 AND the donor lacks capacity for the relevant decisions — both conditions, not either

ends.event: Revocation, disclaimer by the attorney, or removal from the Register
Death of the donor; the estate vests in the personal representatives

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Gevolmachtigde
jurisdictions.summary: A Dutch mandate is durable by omission. Article 3:72 lists what ends a volmacht — death, curatele, bankruptcy, revocation — and the principal's incapacity is not on the list, so a general mandate simply carries on. That is what makes the levenstestament work without any special enduring instrument.

assigned.event: Principal grants a volmacht, the authority to perform juridical acts in the principal's name; in practice recorded in a notarial levenstestament

starts.event: On grant, unless the deed provides otherwise; no registration and no capacity finding are required

ends.event: Death of the principal
Principal placed under curatele, or bankruptcy, or revocation by the principal — but not the onset of incapacity by itself

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Apoderado con poder preventivo

nameEn.en: Agent holding a preventive power of attorney

jurisdictions.summary: A notarial power whose grantor has added a clause keeping it alive if they later need support. Without that clause a Spanish mandate ends when support measures are established.

assigned.event: Granted in escritura pública before a notary

starts.event: On grant; it continues into incapacity because of the subsistence clause

ends.event: Revocation, or death of the grantor
Automatically where granted to a spouse or partner and cohabitation ceases

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: Fullmaktshavare enligt framtidsfullmakt

nameEn.en: Holder of the continuing power of attorney

citation.cite: Government Offices of Sweden, Administrators, guardians ad litem and continuing powers of attorney (published 8 April 2025)
citation.title: Continuing power of attorney
citation.quote: It is the holder of the continuing power of attorney (proxy) who determines when this occurs.

jurisdictions.summary: A future power of attorney that comes into force when the grantor is permanently unable to look after their affairs. Unusually, it is the attorney who judges whether that point has been reached, unless the document sends the question to a court.

assigned.event: Grantor signs a framtidsfullmakt naming a natural person

starts.event: When the grantor's situation matches 1 §; the attorney assesses this, unless the document requires a court

ends.event: Loses effect so far as godmanskap or förvaltarskap is ordered
Överförmyndaren bars its use for abuse or serious neglect

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under a property and financial affairs lasting power of attorney
localNames: donee of a lasting power of attorney (property and affairs)
jurisdictions.summary: An adult with capacity (the donor) appoints one or more attorneys on the prescribed form. The LPA does not exist, and gives no authority, until the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) registers it. After registration the attorney can act while the donor still has capacity (with the donor's permission) and after the donor loses capacity, unless the donor chose 'only when I don't have mental capacity'.

assigned.event: Donor (18+, with capacity) executes the prescribed LPA form with attorney statements and a certificate provider's certificate

starts.event: On registration by OPG (not before). Usable at once with the donor's permission, unless the donor chose the capacity-only option

ends.event: Donor dies (LPA ends automatically; executors/personal representatives take over)
Donor revokes while having capacity (deed of revocation sent to OPG)

Attorney disclaims, dies or lacks capacity, or the marriage or civil partnership between donor and attorney is dissolved or annulled (unless the LPA says otherwise). This ends that attorney's appointment. It revokes the LPA unless a replacement or a joint-and-several co-attorney remains
Court of Protection determines the power revoked or invalid, or revokes it for fraud or for acts not in the donor's best interests; OPG cancels registration
Donor's bankruptcy or debt relief order revokes the power (suspended during an interim bankruptcy or debt relief restrictions order); attorney's bankruptcy or DRO ends that attorney's appointment

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney (made before 1 October 2007)
jurisdictions.summary: EPAs could not be made after the MCA came into force on 1 October 2007, but earlier ones still work under MCA Sch 4. They cover property and financial affairs only. An EPA can be used before registration while the donor has capacity. Once the attorney believes the donor is or is becoming mentally incapable, the attorney must apply to OPG to register it, and until registration can do only limited acts.

assigned.event: Donor and attorney executed prescribed EPA form before 1 October 2007

starts.event: On execution, as an ordinary power, unless the instrument says otherwise; survives the donor's incapacity

ends.event: Donor dies (OPG cancels registration)
Bankruptcy or debt relief order of donor or attorney
Attorney disclaims (by notice to donor, or to OPG once registration applied for) or dies
Court of Protection revokes (e.g. when exercising deputy powers, or attorney unsuitable) or cancels registration

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney (EPA)
jurisdictions.summary: Northern Ireland still uses EPAs, which cover property and financial affairs only. The attorney can act as soon as the EPA is signed, unless the document says otherwise. Once the donor is or is becoming mentally incapable, the attorney must apply to register it with the High Court (Office of Care and Protection). Until registration, the attorney's authority is suspended except for limited interim acts.

assigned.event: Donor executes an EPA in the prescribed form while capable

starts.event: On signing, unless the instrument sets conditions or restrictions on commencement

ends.event: Donor's incapacity supervenes: authority is suspended (apart from interim acts after applying) until the court registers the instrument
Death or bankruptcy of the donor, or death, incapacity or bankruptcy of the attorney: the court cancels registration
Revocation confirmed by the court, disclaimer notified to the court, or court cancels on fraud/undue pressure/unsuitability
Court exercises Part VIII Mental Health Order powers revoking the power (e.g. controller appointed)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Continuing attorney (continuing power of attorney)
jurisdictions.summary: Someone appointed by the granter to deal with property and financial affairs. The power continues if the granter loses capacity. The attorney has no authority until the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland) registers the document. The document can let the attorney act as soon as it is registered, or only once the granter is found incapable.

assigned.event: Granter subscribes a written document with a statement that the power is continuing and a solicitor's (or prescribed person's) certificate of capacity

starts.event: On registration by the Public Guardian, immediately. If the document says so, only once the granter is determined to be incapable (s 15(3)(ba)). Registration itself can be deferred until a specified event (s 19(3)).

ends.event: Death of the granter (common-law end of agency, stated by OPG Scotland; the Act has no express death-termination section for attorneys)
Bankruptcy of the granter or attorney (or protected trust deed, per OPG)
Decree of separation, divorce or nullity (or civil partnership equivalent) between granter and attorney, unless the document says otherwise
Attorney resigns: takes effect 28 days after OPG receives notice (immediately if a joint/substitute attorney is willing)
Guardian appointed with powers over the same matter
Granter revokes by registered revocation notice (needs capacity certificate), or sheriff revokes

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An adult (19 or older) names an attorney to manage financial affairs, and the document must say the authority continues despite incapability. It can take effect as soon as it is signed, or on a stated date or confirmed event such as incapability. It ends on the adult's death, revocation, a court order, a Patients Property Act committee order, or events affecting the attorney.

assigned.event: Capable adult signs the enduring power of attorney before 2 witnesses (or 1 lawyer or notary witness)

starts.event: Latest of: signing by both the adult and the attorney, a stated effective date, or confirmation of a stated triggering event (e.g. incapability confirmed as the document directs, or by a qualified health care provider if the named person cannot act)

ends.event: Adult dies
Adult revokes (while capable) and gives written notice to each attorney
Court terminates the enduring power of attorney under s 36(5)

Adult becomes a patient by court declaration under the Patients Property Act (terminated), or a statutory property guardianship begins and the Public Guardian and Trustee decides to manage the property (suspended, then terminated)

The attorney's authority ends: attorney resigns, dies, becomes incapable or bankrupt, is convicted of a prescribed offence or one against the adult, or is the adult's spouse and they separate (unless the document says otherwise)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under a continuing power of attorney for property
localNames: continuing power of attorney for property (CPOA)
jurisdictions.summary: A property power of attorney is 'continuing' (survives incapacity) only if it says so or shows that intention. It is signed before two qualified witnesses. It lets the attorney do anything with property the grantor could do except make a will. Unless it postpones its effect, it can be used as soon as it is validly signed. It ends at death.

assigned.event: Grantor with capacity under s 8 signs a CPOA before two witnesses who are not disqualified

starts.event: On execution, unless the document postpones effect to a specified date or contingency (see on-cpoa-springing)
starts.note: The SDA has no clause saying 'effective on signing'. That default follows from s 7(7), which makes postponement optional.

ends.event: Grantor dies
Grantor revokes in writing, executed like a CPOA
Grantor executes a new CPOA, unless multiple CPOAs are provided for
Court appoints a guardian of property under s 22
Attorney dies, becomes incapable of managing property or resigns, unless a joint attorney remains or a substitute is named and willing

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandatary under a protection mandate (administration of property)
jurisdictions.summary: The property side of the protection mandate: the mandatary administers the mandator's patrimony. Québec has no enduring power of attorney that works without a court step. Authority starts only on homologation after incapacity is shown, and an ordinary mandate already in place continues during the proceedings. It ends on restored capacity, revocation or death.

assigned.event: Protection mandate signed (notarial or before witnesses)

starts.event: Homologation after incapacity is ascertained

ends.event: Court ascertains restored capacity
Mandator's death; mandatary renders account to the liquidator's side and completes urgent acts
Court revocation; tutorship to property instituted to replace or complete it

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs the power of attorney (acknowledgment before a notary creates a presumption of genuineness)

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

ends.event: Death of principal (good-faith acts without actual knowledge still bind successors)
Revocation by principal; POA terms; purpose accomplished
Agent dies, becomes incapacitated, resigns, or (spouse-agent) dissolution/annulment/legal separation action filed
Court limits, suspends, or terminates authority after appointment of a conservator

jurisdictions.label: US — California
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under durable power of attorney
agent under Uniform Statutory Form Power of Attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal executes a written POA containing the §4124 durability language (or uses the Uniform Statutory Form POA, Prob. Code §4400 et seq.)

starts.event: On execution unless the instrument makes it springing (see financial-poa-springing)
starts.note: California's default 'effective on execution' rule for a non-springing POA was inferred from §4030 (springing defined as the exception); the form language in §4401 is not online.

ends.event: Death of principal, except specific authority permitted by statute after death; good-faith acts without knowledge of death still bind
Revocation, removal, resignation, agent's death or incapacity, dissolution/annulment of marriage to principal, terms of POA
Conservator of the estate revokes or amends, but only after an order of the conservatorship court

jurisdictions.label: US — Florida
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs before two subscribing witnesses and acknowledges before a notary; power is durable only if it contains the statutory durability words or similar words

starts.event: Exercisable when executed (post-10/1/2011 powers cannot be springing)

ends.event: Death of principal
Court adjudicates principal totally or partially incapacitated, unless the court preserves specific authority
Revocation by later power of attorney or other signed writing
Filing of action for dissolution, annulment or legal separation where agent is principal's spouse (unless POA provides otherwise)

jurisdictions.label: US — Illinois
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under statutory short form power of attorney for property
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs; statutory short form requires at least one witness and notarization of principal's signature

starts.event: Statutory form: effective when signed unless a later date or event is specified

ends.event: Death of principal
Earlier termination date or event stated in the agency
Amendment or revocation by principal with capacity, in any manner communicated to agent or a related person
Judgment of dissolution or legal separation: agent-spouse deemed to have died at time of judgment
Court orders guardian to exercise principal's powers, including revocation

jurisdictions.label: US — Louisiana
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal and mandatary conclude a contract of mandate; it is an agreement, not a unilateral grant

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

ends.event: Death of either party, interdiction of the mandatary, or qualification of a curator after the principal's interdiction

jurisdictions.label: US — Maine
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under a durable power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs the power of attorney and acknowledges it before a notary public; a durable power is invalid unless it also carries the statutory Notice to the Principal and Notice to the Agent

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

ends.event: Death of principal (good-faith acts without actual knowledge still bind successors)
Revocation by principal; POA terms; purpose accomplished
Agent dies, becomes incapacitated, resigns, or (spouse-agent) dissolution/annulment/legal separation action filed
Court limits, suspends, or terminates authority after appointment of a conservator

localNames: attorney in fact under a durable power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs a writing containing words showing the authority survives disability

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

assigned.event: Principal signs a power of attorney that is either acknowledged before a notary or signed before two witnesses who also sign

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under statutory short form power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal with capacity signs, initials and dates; signature acknowledged and witnessed by two non-agent witnesses; POA substantially conforms to statutory 'Caution to the Principal' and 'Important Information for the Agent'

starts.event: As to each agent, the date the AGENT's signature is acknowledged (co-agents acting together: when all have signed and acknowledged)

ends.event: Principal dies
Principal revokes; agent dies, becomes incapacitated or resigns; purpose accomplished; divorce/annulment ends spouse-agent authority unless POA provides otherwise
Court revokes under GOL §5-1510 or in an Article 81 guardianship (MHL §81.29(d))

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal executes a power of attorney under Chapter 32C

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under a durable power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Principal signs a written power of attorney; durability is the default and must be opted out of

starts.event: Effective when executed unless the POA states a future date or contingency; agency duties attach when the agent accepts by acting or other conduct

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under durable financial power of attorney
localNames: agent under statutory durable power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A person the principal appoints in a signed power of attorney to act on property and financial matters. Under the UPOAA a power is durable (survives the principal's incapacity) unless it expressly says otherwise, and it ends at the principal's death.

assigned.event: Adult principal signs a writing with durability words and acknowledges it before a notary or other authorized officer

starts.event: Immediately unless the principal selects 'effective upon my disability or incapacity'

ends.event: Principal dies
Principal revokes; POA's own termination terms; purpose accomplished; no agent remains
Permanent guardian of the estate qualifies (automatic revocation unless court orders suspension)

ends.event: Principal's incapacity, unless the writing carries durability words

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An attorney for legal and financial affairs whose power continues after the principal loses mental capacity. The instrument must say so, and must be witnessed and certified by a prescribed witness such as a lawyer or Local Court registrar. The attorney has no authority until they accept by signing. The prescribed form lets the principal choose when it operates, including only once a doctor certifies incapacity.

assigned.event: Principal signs an instrument expressed to continue despite loss of capacity. A prescribed witness (not an attorney) witnesses it and certifies they explained it and the principal appeared to understand.

starts.event: When the attorney accepts by signing (at execution or later), and then from the commencement chosen in the form: on acceptance (default), once a medical practitioner considers the principal unable to manage their affairs, once the attorney considers help is needed, or another event

ends.event: Revocation by the principal while they have capacity. Once NCAT or the Supreme Court declares the principal incapable, the principal cannot lawfully revoke.
Revoked in whole or part by NCAT or the Supreme Court on review
Suspended while the principal's estate is under a financial management order (managed estate), unless the Tribunal keeps it in force for excluded property. The Supreme Court may terminate it.

Vacancy of the only attorney (death, resignation, bankruptcy, loss of capacity or revocation of the attorney), or of one joint attorney unless the instrument provides otherwise and a substitute exists

Death of the principal. There is no express termination section: the rule comes from general law, which the Act assumes (only irrevocable powers are saved from death by s 16) and which NSW Government guidance states.
Bankruptcy of the principal (general law; the Act says so only indirectly, by saving irrevocable powers from bankruptcy)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Queensland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney for financial matters under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An adult with capacity may appoint attorneys for financial matters in the approved form. The principal may say when financial power starts, including on impaired capacity. If nothing is stated, it starts when the document is made. It survives impaired capacity. Death revokes it. Later marriage or civil partnership revokes it except for the new spouse or partner. Divorce or ending a civil partnership revokes it as to the former spouse or partner.

assigned.event: Adult principal with capacity signs approved form before an eligible witness; attorney accepts by signing

starts.event: Time, circumstance or occasion stated in the document; if none stated, once made; if the principal loses capacity before a stated later start, during impaired capacity

ends.event: Death of principal
Principal later marries or enters a civil partnership (revoked except as to new spouse or civil partner, unless contrary intention)
Principal divorces or civil partnership is terminated (revoked as to former spouse or partner)
Written revocation by principal with capacity, or a later inconsistent enduring document
Attorney resigns, dies, loses capacity or becomes bankrupt (as to that attorney)
Supreme Court or QCAT removes attorney or revokes document

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney for financial matters under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An adult with decision-making capacity can appoint an attorney for financial matters in the prescribed form. The principal chooses when the power starts. It can start at once, when the principal loses capacity, or at another time or event. If the document says nothing, it starts as soon as the document is made. Loss of capacity does not end it, but death does. The attorney cannot run the estate after death.

assigned.event: Principal with decision-making capacity signs the prescribed form before two witnesses, one authorised to witness affidavits or a medical practitioner; the attorney signs a witnessed acceptance

starts.event: On the time, circumstance or occasion specified (e.g. immediately, or when the principal ceases to have decision making capacity). If nothing is specified, on the making of the power. If capacity is lost before a specified later start, the power becomes exercisable during the incapacity.

ends.event: Death of the principal
Principal (with capacity) revokes it, or makes a later enduring power of attorney (unless it says otherwise)
Revoked according to its own terms

As to that attorney: the attorney dies, loses capacity, becomes insolvent under administration, becomes a care worker/health/accommodation provider for the principal, is convicted of a dishonesty offence, or resigns
VCAT declares it invalid or revokes it

jurisdictions.label: Mauritius
jurisdictions.roleName: Exécuteur testamentaire
jurisdictions.summary: Named by the testator. The executor seals the estate where there are minor, protected or absent heirs, has the inventory made in the presence of the presumptive heir, and provokes the sale of movables where there is not enough money to meet the legacies. A minor cannot serve, even with a guardian’s authority.

assigned.event: Testator names an exécuteur testamentaire; a minor cannot serve, even authorised by a tuteur or curateur

starts.event: On death, the executor seals the estate where heirs are minor, under tutelle or absent, and has the inventory made in the presence of the presumptive heir

ends.event: Inventory made, movables sold where necessary and the will carried out

jurisdictions.label: Rwanda
jurisdictions.roleName: Testamentary executor
jurisdictions.summary: The testator may name one or several testamentary executors in the will, responsible for liquidating the estate. Where the will names none, an executor is appointed under the law instead — so the office is filled either way.

assigned.event: Testator appoints one or several testamentary executors in the will, responsible for liquidating the estate

starts.event: On the opening of the succession; where the testator named nobody, an executor is appointed under the law

ends.event: Estate liquidated, the acts being approved by the succession council

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor testamentary
jurisdictions.summary: An executor nominated by will. Authority comes from the Master of the High Court issuing letters of executorship on written application, not from the will alone.

assigned.event: Nominated as executor by a will that has been registered and accepted in the office of the Master

starts.event: Master issues letters of executorship on written application

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor of a will (遗嘱执行人)
jurisdictions.summary: A natural person may make a will disposing of their property and may name an executor in it, and may set up a testamentary trust. The will can be withdrawn or varied at any time, and a later inconsistent act counts as a withdrawal. Once succession opens, the named executor is the estate administrator, so the duties are those of that office.

assigned.event: The testator names an executor in a will, and may also set up a testamentary trust

starts.event: Succession opens on death, and the executor is the estate administrator

ends.event: The testator withdraws or varies the will, or performs an act contrary to it, which counts as a withdrawal of the relevant content
The duties of the office are discharged: the estate is cleared, reported, protected, its debts dealt with and the estate divided

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor
jurisdictions.summary: Probate is granted only to an executor appointed by the will. The executor is the deceased’s legal representative for all purposes and the property vests in them — but neither that vesting nor the need for probate applies uniformly: property passing by survivorship is excluded, and s 213 does not apply to wills made by Muslims or Indian Christians.

assigned.event: Testator appoints an executor by the will, expressly or by necessary implication

starts.event: On grant of probate; no right as executor can be established in court without it, subject to the exemptions in s 213(2)

ends.event: Administration of the estate completed

jurisdictions.label: Japan
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor of a will (遺言執行者)
jurisdictions.summary: Designated by the testator in the will, or by a third party the testator entrusts with the choice. The executor holds the right and duty to do everything necessary to realise the will — and where there is an executor, only the executor may perform a bequest.

assigned.event: Testator designates one or more executors in the will, or entrusts the designation to a third party who must then designate and notify the heirs without delay

starts.event: On the commencement of inheritance; the executor manages the estate and does everything necessary to realise the will

ends.event: The content of the will is realised

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor
jurisdictions.summary: Probate may be granted to any executor appointed by a will, and the appointment may be express or implied. Where a will appoints several, probate may issue to one or more without prejudice to a later grant to the others.

assigned.event: Will appoints an executor, expressly or by implication

starts.event: On the grant of probate; where several are appointed, probate may be granted to one or more of them

ends.event: Administration of the estate completed

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor of a will
jurisdictions.summary: Designated in the will, or by a third person the testator commissions. Where nobody is designated, the heir is the executor by operation of law. The executor manages the property given by will and does what is needed to carry it out.

assigned.event: Testator designates an executor by will, or commissions a third person to designate one

starts.event: On the testator’s death the executor holds the right and duty to manage the bequeathed property and to perform the acts necessary to carry out the will

ends.event: The acts necessary to carry out the will are performed

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Bobestyrer indsat ved testamente
jurisdictions.summary: Denmark's nearest equivalent to an executor: the deceased may direct in a will that the estate be administered by a bobestyrer, which is one of the grounds for release.

assigned.event: The deceased so directed by will

starts.event: On the court releasing the estate on that ground

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Testamentin toimeenpanija

citation.cite: Code of Inheritance 40/1965 ch 19 heading (amendments up to 1228/2001)
citation.title: Code of Inheritance (unofficial translation published on Finlex)
citation.quote: Chapter 19 — Administrator of an estate and executor of a testament

jurisdictions.summary: Someone appointed by will to administer the estate in place of the heirs and universal legatees; they too may apply for the administration order.

assigned.event: Appointed by will to hold the estate in place of the heirs

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Exécuteur testamentaire
jurisdictions.summary: Named by will to see to the execution of the testator's wishes, layered on top of the heirs' automatic seisin. Once accepted the office is binding, and its powers die with the holder.

assigned.event: Testator names one or more executors having full civil capacity

starts.event: On death and acceptance of the mission, which the executor is then bound to carry out

ends.event: Mission completed; the powers are not transmissible on death of the executor

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Testamentsvollstrecker

citation.title: Act on Proceedings in Family Matters and in Matters of Non-contentious Jurisdiction (official English translation, as amended to 7 April 2025)
citation.quote: In proceedings for the appointment of an executor and for the issuance of an executor’s certificate, the executor is a participant.

jurisdictions.summary: An executor exists only where the testator appointed one by will. He administers the estate and may dispose of its assets, displacing the heirs' control.

assigned.event: Appointed by the testator in a will

starts.event: On acceptance of the office after death

ends.event: Office completed or falls away

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor
jurisdictions.summary: The estate vests in the personal representatives at the moment of death, before any grant, and they hold it as trustees for those entitled.

assigned.event: Testator names an executor in a will

starts.event: On death the estate devolves on and vests in the personal representatives, notwithstanding any testamentary disposition; the grant of probate proves the title

ends.event: Administration completed and the estate distributed to those entitled

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor of a will (esecutore testamentario)
jurisdictions.summary: The testator may name one or more executors, and substitutes for any who will not or cannot accept. The executor must see that the last wishes are exactly carried out, is joined in actions concerning the estate during their management, must account at the end of it, and may be removed by the court for grave irregularity. Expenses of the office fall on the estate.

assigned.event: The testator names one or more executors in the will, and may name substitutes for any who will not or cannot accept

starts.event: The executor takes up the office and must see that the deceased’s last wishes are exactly carried out; actions concerning the estate are brought against the executor as well during the management

ends.event: The executor accounts for the management at its end, and in any event once a year has passed since the testator’s death
The court removes the executor from office for grave irregularity, on the application of any interested party

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Executeur
jurisdictions.summary: Appointed only by will, and layered on top of the heirs' automatic succession rather than replacing it. Where there are several, each may act alone unless the testator said otherwise.

assigned.event: Testator appoints one or more executeurs by testamentary disposition

starts.event: On death and acceptance of the office; the heirs have already succeeded of right

ends.event: Administration completed, or the kantonrechter appoints a replacement where a named executeur is lacking

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Albacea

citation.cite: Spanish Civil Code 2016 (Ministerio de Justicia English translation, consolidated text to 6 October 2015), art 892
citation.title: On executors or administrators (unofficial translation published by the Ministry of Justice; law as of 6 Oct 2015)
citation.quote: The testator may appoint one or more executors.

jurisdictions.summary: An executor exists only if the testator named one; the heirs otherwise hold the estate directly.

assigned.event: Named by the testator

starts.event: On death and acceptance of the office

ends.event: Office discharged

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: Testamentsexekutor

citation.cite: Domstolsverket, Svensk/engelsk ordlista – Swedish/English Glossary (March 2019), entry testamentsexekutor
citation.title: Swedish/English Glossary

jurisdictions.summary: Someone named in a will to administer the estate in place of the heirs and universal legatees; they may also ask the court for an administration order.

assigned.event: Named by will to take the heirs' place in administering the estate

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Administration completed

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor
localNames: executor to whom probate is granted
jurisdictions.summary: An executor is named in the will. Their title and authority come from the will and start at the moment of death. The grant of probate from the High Court (Family Division probate registry) does not create that authority. It is the only way to prove it, and most asset holders ask to see it.

assigned.event: Testator names executor in a valid will

starts.event: At the testator's death: estate vests in the executor; may act (and even start proceedings) before probate, but needs the grant to prove title

ends.event: Estate fully administered: debts, taxes and legacies paid, residue distributed. No formal discharge exists
Executor gives up the right to apply for probate (renunciation, form PA15) or holds power reserved
Grant revoked, or court passes over the executor and appoints an administrator in special circumstances

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor (grant of probate)
jurisdictions.summary: The executor named in the will has first priority for a grant of probate from the Probate Office (High Court). The deceased's real and personal estate vests in the personal representatives. The executor should distribute as soon as reasonably practicable, and beneficiaries normally cannot sue for non-distribution within the first year.

assigned.event: Testator names executor in will

starts.event: Executor's title derives from the will at death. Most asset holders require the grant of probate.

ends.event: Estate distributed

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor-nominate (with confirmation)
jurisdictions.summary: The executor named in the will, or failing one, the testamentary trustees, then a general disponee or universal or residuary legatee. The executor lodges an inventory at the sheriff court and obtains confirmation, which vests the estate in them for administration.

assigned.event: Testator names an executor in the will (or s 3 of the 1900 Act supplies one)

starts.event: On confirmation by the sheriff court. Banks and other holders typically require confirmation before releasing assets.

ends.event: Estate ingathered and distributed (no statutory discharge step located)
If all confirmed executors die or become incapable, confirmation becomes inoperative. Remaining estate needs confirmation ad non executa.

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Executor (grant of probate)
jurisdictions.summary: The executor named in a will gets authority from the will at death, and the estate vests in the executor on assuming office. To deal with most assets the executor applies to the Supreme Court for a grant of probate. The executor must first deliver notice (Form P1) to beneficiaries and others, then wait at least 21 days. The grant gives exclusive authority, and the executor is finished when discharged by the court.

jurisdictions.summary: A testator may designate one or more liquidators. Anyone so designated, whether called executor or administrator, is a liquidator. A notarial will needs no probate, but a holograph or witnessed will must first be probated by the court or a notary. Liquidation ends with the final account and discharge.

ends.event: Liquidator declines office (not bound to accept unless sole heir)

A divorce, annulment, end of a civil partnership or end of a de facto relationship revokes the former partner's appointment as executor unless the will shows a contrary intention. Marriage revokes the whole will, with exceptions.

Marriage revokes the whole will, except a will made in contemplation of that marriage.

localNames: guardianship of an adult with mental disability
jurisdictions.summary: A court declares that an adult with mental disability be provided with a guardian. What stands out is the procedure: the court appoints only after hearing and observing the person themselves, hearing witnesses and the family council, and examining medical records of that person’s mental health.

assigned.event: A parent, a spouse, or the adult themselves applies for a guardian to be provided

starts.event: The competent court declares that the adult be provided with a guardian and appoints one, after hearing and observing the person, hearing witnesses and the family council, and examining medical records

ends.event: Death of the adult, which opens the succession

jurisdictions.roleName: Designated guardian (指定监护人)
jurisdictions.summary: Where who should be guardian is disputed, the residents’ or villagers’ committee or the civil affairs department designates one, and a party dissatisfied with that designation — or any party directly — may apply to the People’s Court. If the ward’s rights would otherwise be unprotected while the designation is pending, the committee, a body provided by law or the civil affairs department serves as interim guardian.

assigned.event: The choice of guardian is disputed, or nobody is qualified to serve

starts.event: The committee or civil affairs department designates a guardian, or the People’s Court does so on application; the designation may not then be changed at will

ends.event: The guardianship relationship terminates under art 39
A parent or child whose qualification was revoked is restored by the court, and the designated guardian’s relationship terminates at the same time

jurisdictions.roleName: Limited guardian
jurisdictions.summary: Support comes first. A district court or designated authority may add a limited guardian only where the person has already been given adequate and appropriate support and is still unable to take legally binding decisions — and that guardian decides in consultation with the person.

assigned.event: District court or designated authority finds that a person given adequate and appropriate support is still unable to take legally binding decisions

starts.event: Further support of a limited guardian is provided, to take legally binding decisions on the person’s behalf in consultation with them

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.summary: The heaviest of Japan’s three tiers, for a person constantly lacking the capacity to appreciate their situation. The guardian manages property and represents the ward in juristic acts — but must respect the ward’s wishes and have regard to their mental and physical state and their circumstances of life.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates the commencement of guardianship on application by the person, spouse, a relative within the fourth degree, an existing guardian or supervisor, or a public prosecutor

starts.event: The Family Court appoints an adult guardian of its own motion when it adjudicates commencement; the guardian manages property and represents the ward in juristic acts concerning it

ends.event: The cause has ceased and the Family Court rescinds the adjudication of commencement
Death of the ward, which commences the inheritance

assigned.event: Court finds P lacks capacity in relation to personal welfare and appoints a deputy rather than deciding the matter itself

starts.event: On appointment, within the powers the order confers

ends.event: Death of P

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Adult guardian
jurisdictions.summary: Appointed by the Family Court for a person who continuously lacks the capacity to manage affairs. The guardian is the ward’s legal representative, but the court sets how far that representation reaches and how far the guardian may decide personal affairs.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of adult guardianship on application by the principal, spouse, a relative within the fourth degree, a public prosecutor or the head of a local government

starts.event: An adult guardian is appointed once commencement is adjudged; the guardian becomes legal representative within the scope the court sets

ends.event: Family Court adjudicates termination once the cause for commencement has ceased
Death of the ward; the estate passes to the heirs by universal succession

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Personne habilitée (habilitation familiale)
jurisdictions.summary: A lighter family route added in 2016: the court empowers a relative once, and the measure then runs without the continuing judicial supervision that tutelle and curatelle carry.

assigned.event: Family member applies where the person cannot see to their own interests because of a medically established impairment

starts.event: Court grants the habilitation to represent or assist the person, for specified acts or generally

ends.event: Habilitation revoked or expires
Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Rechtlicher Betreuer (Personensorge)
jurisdictions.summary: A court-appointed legal supporter. Subsidiary to a valid power of attorney, never against the adult's free will, and bound to give effect to their wishes.

assigned.event: Betreuungsgericht appoints, on the adult's application or of its own motion

starts.event: On appointment, only so far as necessary

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Decision-making representative (personal welfare)
jurisdictions.summary: The court's last resort for personal welfare, available only where no co-decision-maker is suitable or registered. Ireland has no guardianship: the court appoints a representative for specified decisions.

assigned.event: Court declares the person lacks capacity and no suitable or registered co-decision-maker exists

starts.event: Court order appointing a decision-making representative for specified personal welfare decisions

ends.event: Court varies or discharges the order, or the representative is disqualified
Death of the relevant person

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Committee of a ward (being wound down)
jurisdictions.summary: Wardship is abolished prospectively. Every adult ward must be reviewed by the wardship court and discharged into the 2015 Act's tiers, so this role only shrinks.

assigned.event: Person was taken into wardship under the pre-2023 jurisdiction

starts.event: Committee appointed by the wardship court under the former jurisdiction

ends.event: Wardship court reviews the ward's capacity and declares either that the ward does not lack capacity or that a 2015 Act arrangement applies, discharging the ward from wardship
Death of the ward

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Guardian of an interdicted person (tutore dell’interdetto)
jurisdictions.summary: The heaviest measure, for an adult in a condition of habitual infirmity of mind that makes them incapable of seeing to their own interests, where interdiction is necessary to ensure adequate protection. The rules on guardianship of minors apply to the guardian of the interdicted person.

assigned.event: An adult or emancipated minor in a condition of habitual infirmity of mind making them incapable of attending to their own interests is interdicted, where that is necessary for adequate protection

starts.event: The provisions on guardianship of minors apply to the guardianship of the interdicted person

ends.event: The measure is revoked and, where the conditions are met, replaced by support administration

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Mentor
jurisdictions.summary: The mirror image of bewind: mentorschap covers interests of a non-property nature only, so care and treatment decisions sit here while money sits with the bewindvoerder.

assigned.event: Application to the kantonrechter for mentorschap

starts.event: Kantonrechter institutes mentorschap where the adult cannot properly look after interests of a non-property nature

ends.event: Mentorschap terminated by the kantonrechter
Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: Sweden
jurisdictions.roleName: God man
