citation.title: Administrators
citation.quote: An administrator may not be appointed if it would be sufficient to appoint a guardian ad litem (god man)

jurisdictions.summary: A court or the chief guardian orders godmanskap where illness or a weakened state means someone needs help with financial or personal matters, and generally only with their consent.

assigned.event: Godmanskap ordered where the person needs help and no lesser measure suffices

starts.event: On the order

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Personal welfare (health and welfare) deputy
jurisdictions.summary: The Court of Protection can appoint a deputy for health and welfare decisions. It does so less often, because the court prefers to make single decisions itself. A welfare deputy cannot refuse life-sustaining treatment, stop named people contacting P, or hand P's healthcare responsibility to a different person.

assigned.event: Court of Protection order under MCA s 16

starts.event: When the court order is sent to the deputy

ends.event: P dies: the deputyship ends (deputy tells OPG and the court; the final report may be required)
P regains capacity: the deputy loses power over matters P can decide, and the order is discharged on application (form COP9)
Court revokes the appointment or varies/discharges the order (e.g. deputy acting outside authority or not in P's best interests), or order expires
Deputy steps down (court order needed) or dies (sole/joint deputyship ends)

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Person authorised under an intervention order
localNames: person authorised under an intervention order
jurisdictions.summary: For a single decision or action (financial, property or welfare), the sheriff can make an intervention order instead of a full guardianship. The order either directs the action or authorises a named person to take it. It is used for one-off matters, such as selling a house.

assigned.event: Sheriff makes the order on application by anyone claiming an interest (or by the local authority where needed)

starts.event: On the sheriff's order. The Public Guardian registers it.

ends.event: The specified action is completed, or the sheriff varies or recalls the order
Death of the adult: the order ceases to have effect. A person acting in good faith before learning of the death is protected.

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Guardian with personal welfare powers
jurisdictions.summary: A guardian appointed by the sheriff to make personal welfare decisions, which can include medical treatment. The local authority supervises, and the Mental Welfare Commission also has a role. A guardian cannot authorise donation under the Human Tissue (Scotland) Act 2006.

assigned.event: Sheriff grants a guardianship order on application (adult incapable and likely to remain so; no other AWI measure sufficient)

starts.event: On the order. The Public Guardian registers the appointment and issues a certificate of appointment (after caution/security is found, if required).

ends.event: Order expires at the end of its period (3 years by default, or another period including indefinite) unless renewed. It continues while a renewal application is pending.
Sheriff recalls the order, or replaces/removes the guardian
Public Guardian (financial powers) or local authority/Mental Welfare Commission (welfare powers) recalls the powers
Guardian resigns
Death of the adult: the guardianship order ceases to have effect

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Committee of the person (Patients Property Act)
jurisdictions.summary: On a court declaration, supported by 2 medical affidavits, that an adult cannot manage themself, the Supreme Court appoints a committee with custody of the person. The Public Guardian and Trustee is committee when no one else is appointed. The appointment terminates the adult's powers of attorney and, unless the court orders otherwise, their representation agreements. It ends when the court declares the person no longer incapable, or on discharge.

assigned.event: Supreme Court declares the adult incapable of managing himself or herself and appoints a committee (adult's own written nomination must be followed absent good reason)

starts.event: On the court order

ends.event: Court declares the patient no longer incapable (application after 1 year, or sooner by leave), then committee discharged
Court rescinds the appointment or appoints a successor committee
Patient dies: custody of the person has no further object; committee accounts to the executor or administrator and may be discharged

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Court-appointed guardian of the person
jurisdictions.summary: On any person's application, the court may appoint a guardian of the person for someone incapable of personal care who needs decisions made, unless a less restrictive alternative would do. The guardian ranks first in the HCCA consent hierarchy, and the appointment ends any power of attorney for personal care.

assigned.event: Court order under s 55

starts.event: On appointment

ends.event: Court terminates the guardianship on motion (powers may be suspended pending the motion)
Person dies (no express SDA termination-on-death clause for court guardianship of the person was found)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Tutor to the person of full age
jurisdictions.summary: Since 1 November 2022 tutorship is Québec's only court protective regime for adults; curatorship and advisers were abolished. The court institutes tutorship when an adult cannot care for themself and needs representation. A tutor may be appointed to the person, to property, or both, and the court tailors the scope. The Public Curator acts only if appointed or if no tutor remains. Tutorship ends on a judgment of release or the adult's death.

assigned.event: Court (or notary under CCP art 312) institutes tutorship and appoints tutor to the person

starts.event: On the judgment

ends.event: Judgment of release, or expiry of the period to contest a report attesting that incapacity or need for representation has ceased
Death of the person of full age

jurisdictions.roleName: Representante del incapaz

nameEn.en: Legal representative of a person lacking capacity

jurisdictions.summary: Incapacity restricts legal personality but does not remove it: the person exercises rights and takes on obligations through their legal representative.

assigned.event: By the incapacity regime, through a legal representative

starts.event: When the incapacity applies

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.summary: A personal decision-maker appointed by a plenary or limited, continuing or temporary guardianship order of the Civil and Administrative Tribunal. jurisdictions.summary: QCAT may appoint a guardian for personal matters, including health matters, if the adult has impaired capacity for the matter, a decision is needed or there is unreasonable risk, and the adult's needs or interests would not otherwise be met. The appointment ends automatically when the adult dies, among other events. QCAT reviews it at least every 5 years.

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Guardian appointed by VCAT
jurisdictions.summary: VCAT may appoint a guardian for the personal matters specified in an order. It must be satisfied that, because of disability, the person lacks decision-making capacity for those matters, needs a guardian, and that the order will promote their wellbeing. The guardian cannot manage the estate after death. VCAT must reassess the order within 12 months and at least every 3 years.

assigned.event: VCAT makes a guardianship order (or urgent order) on application

starts.event: On the making of the order, for the personal matters specified

ends.event: VCAT revokes, varies or replaces the order on reassessment

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.roleName: Person mandated in writing to consent
jurisdictions.summary: South Africa has no enduring power of attorney, but the National Health Act lets a user mandate someone in writing to give informed consent to health services on their behalf once the user cannot give it themselves.

assigned.event: User mandates a person in writing to grant consent on his or her behalf

starts.event: When the user is unable to give informed consent

ends.event: Death of the user

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Nominated representative
jurisdictions.summary: Anyone not a minor may appoint a nominated representative in writing on plain paper, or name one in order of precedence in an advance directive that also says how they wish, or do not wish, to be treated for mental illness.

assigned.event: Person who is not a minor appoints a nominated representative in writing, or names individuals in order of precedence in an advance directive

starts.event: On appointment in writing, signed or thumb-marked, the appointee having accepted

ends.event: Revocation of the appointment

jurisdictions.label: Singapore
jurisdictions.roleName: Donee of a lasting power of attorney (personal welfare)
jurisdictions.summary: The same instrument may confer authority over personal welfare, and it works the same way: created only on registration, exercisable only once P lacks capacity for the decision in question.

assigned.event: P executes an instrument conferring authority over personal welfare on a donee who meets the statutory requirements

starts.event: On registration, and when P no longer has capacity to make the welfare decision

ends.event: P revokes the power at any time while having capacity to do so
Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Personne de confiance
jurisdictions.summary: Designated in writing and co-signed by the designee, consulted when the patient can no longer express their will. Its distinguishing feature is evidential: the personne de confiance reports the patient's wishes and that testimony prevails over any other.

assigned.event: Adult designates a relative, a close person or their doctor in writing; the designation is co-signed by the designee and valid without time limit

starts.event: When the patient is no longer able to express their will and receive the information needed for that purpose

ends.event: Revised or revoked at any time, by either the patient or the personne de confiance
Death of the patient

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Bevollmächtigter in Gesundheitsangelegenheiten
jurisdictions.summary: The same agent acting for health care. Consent to risky measures, confinement and coercive treatment requires written authority that expressly covers them.

assigned.event: Written power of attorney expressly covering health measures

starts.event: On the principal becoming unable to consent

ends.event: Revocation, or death of the principal

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an enduring power (personal welfare)
jurisdictions.summary: The same instrument may cover personal welfare. The 2022 Act repealed the separate welfare-scope section and folded that authority into s 59 itself.

assigned.event: Donor confers authority over all or part of personal welfare in the enduring power

starts.event: Registration under s 69 and the donor's lack of capacity, on the same cumulative test as the property side

ends.event: Revocation, disclaimer or removal from the Register
Death of the donor

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Designated healthcare representative
jurisdictions.summary: Named inside an advance healthcare directive rather than in a separate instrument, and must sign it to accept. Its core power is to ensure the directive is complied with; interpretive and consent powers are optional add-ons.

assigned.event: Directive-maker designates a named individual in an advance healthcare directive, who signs to confirm willingness

starts.event: When the directive applies, on the directive-maker's loss of capacity

ends.event: Directive revoked, or the representative declines or is disqualified
Death of the directive-maker

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Health-care representative under advance directives (fiduciario)
jurisdictions.summary: Under the 2017 law on informed consent and advance directives, an adult may record their wishes about treatment and name a person of trust — the fiduciario — to stand in their place and represent them with the doctor and the health service. If there is no fiduciary, or they decline, die or become incapable, the directives keep their effect and the giudice tutelare may appoint a support administrator if needed.

assigned.event: An adult capable of understanding and willing, anticipating possible future incapacity and after receiving adequate medical information, makes advance directives and names a person of trust to represent them

starts.event: The fiduciary stands in the person’s place with the doctor and the health service; acceptance is by signing the directives or by a later act annexed to them

ends.event: The directives contain no fiduciary, or the fiduciary renounces, dies or becomes incapable — the directives keep their effect and, if needed, the giudice tutelare appoints a support administrator

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Schriftelijk gemachtigde (WGBO)
jurisdictions.summary: A person authorised in writing to stand in the patient's place for treatment decisions. It ranks below a curator or mentor but above the family, and needs only a written authorisation, not a notarial deed.

assigned.event: Patient authorises a person in writing to act in their place

starts.event: When the care provider judges the adult patient incapable of a reasonable appraisal of their interests, and no curatele or mentorschap is in place

ends.event: Curatele or mentorschap instituted, which displaces the written authorisation
Patient regains capacity, or dies

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Representante designado en instrucciones previas
jurisdictions.summary: Through an advance instructions document a person states their treatment wishes and may name a representative; it also covers what happens to the body and organs after death.

assigned.event: Named in the instrucciones previas document

starts.event: When the grantor can no longer express their wishes personally

ends.event: Authority over the body and organs continues past death by the document’s own terms; the document itself may be revoked freely in writing at any time while the grantor can do so

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under a health and welfare lasting power of attorney
localNames: donee of a lasting power of attorney (personal welfare)
LPA for health and care decisions
jurisdictions.summary: A registered health and welfare LPA lets the attorney decide about care, where the donor lives and medical treatment. It works only when the donor lacks capacity for the decision, or the attorney reasonably believes so. The attorney can decide about life-sustaining treatment only if the LPA expressly says so.

assigned.event: Donor (18+, with capacity) executes the prescribed LPA form

starts.event: Registered by OPG AND donor lacks (or attorney reasonably believes donor lacks) capacity for the particular decision

ends.event: Donor dies (LPA ends automatically; executors/personal representatives take over)
Donor revokes while having capacity (deed of revocation sent to OPG)

Attorney disclaims, dies or lacks capacity, or the marriage or civil partnership between donor and attorney is dissolved or annulled (unless the LPA says otherwise). This ends that attorney's appointment. It revokes the LPA unless a replacement or a joint-and-several co-attorney remains
Court of Protection determines the power revoked or invalid, or revokes it for fraud or for acts not in the donor's best interests; OPG cancels registration

jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland
jurisdictions.roleName: Welfare attorney (welfare power of attorney)
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed to make personal welfare decisions, including medical treatment consent. The power must be registered with the OPG, and it can be used only when the granter is incapable of the decision, or the attorney reasonably believes so. A welfare attorney cannot authorise organ or tissue donation for the granter.

assigned.event: Granter subscribes a written document with a welfare-power statement, a statement on how incapacity may be determined, and a certificate

starts.event: After registration AND only while the granter is incapable of the decision, or the attorney reasonably believes so

ends.event: Death of the granter
Decree of separation, divorce or nullity (or civil partnership equivalent), unless document provides otherwise
Attorney resigns (28 days after OPG receives notice)
Guardian appointed with powers over the same matter
Revocation by granter (registered notice) or by sheriff

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Representative under a section 9 (non-standard) representation agreement
jurisdictions.summary: A capable adult can authorize a representative to make personal care and health care decisions, including where to live and giving or refusing life-sustaining treatment. The agreement takes effect on execution unless it names a later triggering event. The representative helps the adult decide or decides for the adult; the representative does not need a finding of incapacity. The agreement ends on the adult's death.

assigned.event: Adult who understands the nature and consequences signs a s 9 agreement before 2 witnesses (or 1 lawyer or notary); representative signs

starts.event: On execution unless the agreement names a later triggering event and says who confirms it. For substitute consent to health care, the health care provider must first be of the opinion that the adult is incapable of consenting.

ends.event: Adult dies
Capable adult revokes with written notice
Court cancels the agreement
Representative resigns, dies or becomes incapable, or spousal relationship ends (unless an alternate or co-representative continues, or the agreement says otherwise)
Adult becomes a patient by court order under the Patients Property Act (unless the court orders otherwise)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney for personal care
localNames: power of attorney for personal care (POAPC)
jurisdictions.summary: A written power of attorney for personal care authorizes an attorney to make personal-care decisions (health care, shelter, nutrition, clothing, hygiene, safety). A provision is effective only when the grantor is incapable. For treatment covered by the HCCA, that means when the health practitioner finds the person incapable. For other decisions, when the attorney has reasonable grounds to believe so, unless the document requires confirmation (by its own method or a capacity assessor).

assigned.event: Grantor with capacity under s 47 signs a written POAPC (two witnesses)

starts.event: Decision by decision. HCCA decisions: when a health practitioner finds the grantor incapable for that treatment and the HCCA gives the attorney authority. Other decisions: when the attorney has reasonable grounds to believe the grantor is incapable, or on assessor confirmation if the POA requires it.

ends.event: Grantor regains capacity for the decision (their own decision governs)
Court appoints a guardian of the person under s 55
Revocation, or execution of a new POAPC unless multiple are provided for
Attorney dies, becomes incapable of personal care or resigns, with no remaining joint attorney or substitute
Grantor dies: personal-care decision-making ends because there is no living grantor to decide for. Section 53 does NOT list the grantor's death (unlike s 12(1)(f) for CPOAs).

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandatary under a protection mandate (protection of the person)
jurisdictions.summary: A person of full age gives a protection mandate in anticipation of incapacity, by notarial act en minute or before 2 witnesses. It has no effect until incapacity is shown by medical and psychosocial assessment reports and the court, or a notary under the CCP, homologates it. The mandatary then consents to care and looks after the person's well-being. It ends when the court finds the mandator capable again, on revocation, or on either party's death.

assigned.event: Mandator signs protection mandate (notarial act en minute or before 2 disinterested witnesses)

starts.event: Homologation by the court (or before a notary under CCP art 312) on proof of incapacity by medical and psychosocial assessments, on application by the designated mandatary

ends.event: Court ascertains mandator has again become capable (presumed if no objection within 30 days after the capacity report is filed)
Death of the mandator or the mandatary (mandatary must notify the Public Curator of the mandator's death)
Court revokes the mandate for unfaithful performance or other serious reason (and may institute tutorship)
Mandatary renounces after arranging replacement or applying for tutorship

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Individual signs power of attorney for health care (2023: in a record with one qualifying adult witness; 1993: signed writing)

starts.event: Finding of lack of capacity under §4(b) or by a court (2023). 1993: primary physician's determination unless the directive says otherwise, or immediately if the POA so specifies

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)
Revocation by principal; spouse-agent divorce/separation events; disqualification

Principal's death: neither UHCDA text expressly addresses this; no post-death powers (autopsy, disposition of remains) are granted. Any post-death anatomical-gift authority comes from Revised UAGA §9(a)(1)

jurisdictions.label: US — California
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: agent under power of attorney for health care
agent under advance health care directive
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Adult having capacity executes a power of attorney for health care (Health Care Decisions Law, Prob. Code §4600 et seq.)

starts.event: Unless the POA provides otherwise, on a determination that the principal lacks capacity, made by the primary physician unless the directive specifies otherwise

ends.event: Determination that the principal has recovered capacity (authority ceases; can resume on a new determination)
Revocation by signed writing or by personally informing the supervising provider
Dissolution or annulment of marriage to the agent
Post-death decisions end once anatomical gift, autopsy, remains disposition and records release are completed
ends.note: §4683(b) allows these post-death decisions; the statute does not state a separate end point.

jurisdictions.label: US — Florida
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: agent under durable power of attorney with health care authority
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Principal signs written designation before two subscribing adult witnesses; surrogate may not witness and one witness must be neither spouse nor blood relative

starts.event: Primary or attending physician determines principal lacks capacity and enters evaluation in record (second physician if in question); or immediately if the document so stipulates

ends.event: Physician determines principal regained capacity (authority ceases but recommences on later incapacity; not applicable to immediately exercisable authority)
Revocation by signed writing, destruction, oral expression, or materially different later directive; effective when communicated
Dissolution or annulment of marriage revokes designation of former spouse
Court in guardianship modifies or revokes surrogate authority
Time of termination stated in the document

jurisdictions.label: US — Illinois
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: agent under power of attorney for health care
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Principal signs health care agency witnessed by one adult who is not a restricted person; agent is 18+ and not the treating provider

starts.event: Statutory form default: when principal cannot make decisions as determined by treating physician(s) (lack of decisional capacity); optional immediate access to records and communication with providers

ends.event: Revocation at any time regardless of mental or physical condition (unless 30-day delayed revocation elected)
Judgment of dissolution or legal separation with agent-spouse
After death: continues only as necessary for anatomical gift, autopsy, disposition of remains, access to medical records, and pending benefits applications while no executor or administrator

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: person designated to make a declaration
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. assigned.event: Designation in writing by an individual 18 or older of sound mind; the patient advocate must accept before acting

starts.event: The attending physician and a second physician or licensed psychologist determine on examination that the patient cannot participate in treatment decisions, in writing and in the medical record

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)
Revocation by principal; spouse-agent divorce/separation events; disqualification

starts.event: The directive is transmitted to the attending physician or health care institution AND the patient is determined to lack capacity for the particular decision

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)

jurisdictions.label: US — New York
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Competent adult signs and dates health care proxy before two adult witnesses (agent cannot witness)

starts.event: Attending practitioner determines, in writing and to a reasonable degree of medical certainty, that principal lacks capacity; consultation required for certain decisions or conditions; notice to principal and agent

ends.event: Attending practitioner determines principal regained capacity
Revocation (oral, written or any act showing specific intent); divorce or legal separation from spouse-agent unless proxy specifies otherwise
Expiration date or condition stated in the proxy
Death, except that the agent ranks first to make an anatomical gift of the decedent's body

jurisdictions.label: US — North Carolina
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: attorney-in-fact under a health care power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Individual signs power of attorney for health care (2023: in a record with one qualifying adult witness; 1993: signed writing)

starts.event: Physicians designated by the principal determine in writing that the principal lacks sufficient understanding or capacity to make or communicate health care decisions

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)
Revocation by principal; spouse-agent divorce/separation events; disqualification

Principal's death: neither UHCDA text expressly addresses this; no post-death powers (autopsy, disposition of remains) are granted. Any post-death anatomical-gift authority comes from Revised UAGA §9(a)(1)

jurisdictions.label: US — Ohio
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: attorney in fact under a durable power of attorney for health care

The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Adult of sound mind executes a durable power of attorney for health care

starts.event: When the principal's attending physician determines the principal has lost the capacity to make informed health care decisions

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)
Revocation by principal; spouse-agent divorce/separation events; disqualification

Principal's death: neither UHCDA text expressly addresses this; no post-death powers (autopsy, disposition of remains) are granted. Any post-death anatomical-gift authority comes from Revised UAGA §9(a)(1)

assigned.event: Individual signs power of attorney for health care (2023: in a record with one qualifying adult witness; 1993: signed writing)

starts.event: A copy of the health care power of attorney is given to the attending physician and that physician determines the principal is incompetent

ends.event: Becomes inoperative during any time the attending physician determines the principal is competent

jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under power of attorney for health care
localNames: agent under medical power of attorney

starts.event: Attending physician certifies in writing, filed in the medical record, that the principal is incompetent

ends.event: Revocation by oral or written notice or any act showing intent to revoke, regardless of principal's competence; or a later medical POA
Divorce, annulment or voiding of marriage to agent unless POA provides otherwise
Probate court suspends or revokes agent in guardianship proceeding
Principal's death
ends.note: Subchapter D does not state death as a termination event in the sections reviewed. Post-death control of remains needs a separate §711.002 appointment.

localNames: agent with general authority over health care matters

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Enduring guardian
jurisdictions.summary: A person an adult appoints, by a witnessed instrument the appointee also accepts, to make decisions about where they live, health care, personal services and consent to medical and dental treatment. The appointment operates only while the appointor is a 'person in need of a guardian'. It is revoked automatically if the appointor later marries someone else, and is suspended by any guardianship order.

assigned.event: Adult (18+) signs prescribed-form instrument; appointee endorses acceptance; eligible witness certifies voluntary execution and apparent understanding

starts.event: Only while the appointor is totally or partially incapable of managing their person because of a disability. The appointee may ask NCAT to declare that the appointment has effect.

ends.event: Revocation by the appointor with legal capacity, by prescribed witnessed instrument with written notice to the appointee
Appointor marries or remarries someone other than the appointee
Resignation: by written notice if the appointor is not in need of a guardian, or with Tribunal approval if they are
Revocation by NCAT on review (best interests or at the guardian's request) or by the Supreme Court
Appointor regains capacity: the appointment stops having effect, but revives in any later period of need
Death of the appointor

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Queensland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney for personal (including health) matters under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An enduring power of attorney may give power for personal matters, which include health matters. The principal cannot choose an earlier start: this power is exercisable only while the principal has impaired capacity for the matter. An advance health directive and any QCAT guardian rank ahead of the attorney for health matters.

assigned.event: Adult principal with capacity signs approved form; attorney accepts

starts.event: Only during any or every period the principal has impaired capacity for the matter

ends.event: Principal regains capacity (power not exercisable)
Death of principal
Marriage/civil partnership, divorce/termination, revocation, later document, attorney becomes paid carer or health provider, resignation, court/QCAT order

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Queensland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney appointed by an advance health directive (and the directive itself)
jurisdictions.summary: In an advance health directive, an adult gives directions about future health care, which can include refusing life-sustaining measures. The adult may also appoint attorneys for health matters in case the directions prove inadequate. The document needs a doctor's or nurse practitioner's capacity certificate. Its directions and the attorney's power operate only while the principal has impaired capacity, and a direction takes priority over every other decision maker.

assigned.event: Adult with capacity makes written directive, witnessed, with doctor or nurse practitioner certificate; attorney signs acceptance

starts.event: Only while the principal has impaired capacity for the matter

ends.event: Death of principal
Revocation in writing by principal with capacity, or later inconsistent enduring document
Marriage/civil partnership or divorce/termination (as to attorney appointments)
Court or QCAT revokes or changes

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney for personal matters under an enduring power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: The same enduring power of attorney can cover personal or lifestyle matters, such as where and with whom the principal lives. It cannot cover medical treatment, which is handled by a medical treatment decision maker under the 2016 Act. In Victoria, power over personal matters is not limited by statute to periods of incapacity: the principal sets the start, and the default is on making. It ends at death.

assigned.event: Principal with capacity executes the prescribed form confining or extending power to personal matters; attorney accepts

starts.event: As specified in the instrument (e.g. when the principal ceases to have capacity); otherwise on making

ends.event: Death of the principal
Revocation by the principal or a later enduring power; resignation; death, incapacity or disqualifying event of the attorney
VCAT guardianship order suspends exercise unless VCAT authorises

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Appointed medical treatment decision maker
jurisdictions.summary: An adult with capacity may appoint one or more medical treatment decision makers. The appointment is in force from the date it is made, but it gives no decision-making power while the person can decide. It is used only when the person lacks decision-making capacity for the treatment decision. The appointee then makes the decision the person would have made. It ranks first in the statutory hierarchy.

assigned.event: Adult with capacity signs a written appointment, witnessed and certified; each appointee signs a witnessed acceptance

starts.event: Appointment is in force on the date made, but the power to decide arises only when the person does not have decision-making capacity for the particular treatment decision

ends.event: Person regains decision-making capacity (power not exercisable)
Revocation by the person with capacity, resignation, or VCAT revocation

Death of the person: no treatment decisions remain. The Act has no express provision; after death, tissue donation authority passes to the senior available next of kin under the Human Tissue Act 1982.

jurisdictions.roleName: Persona designada en directivas médicas anticipadas

nameEn.en: Person named in advance medical directives

jurisdictions.summary: A fully capable person may issue advance directives and confer a mandate about their health in anticipation of their own incapacity, and may name who is to give consent to medical acts and to act as curator. Directives amounting to euthanasia are treated as unwritten.

assigned.event: Fully capable person anticipates directives and designates the person who is to express consent to medical acts and to exercise the curatela

starts.event: In anticipation of the grantor’s own incapacity

ends.event: Death of the grantor

jurisdictions.roleName: Applicant for a deceased patient's health records
localNames: person who may have a claim arising out of the patient's death
jurisdictions.summary: Data protection law covers only living people, so a deceased patient's records are reached through separate statutes. In England, Wales and Scotland the Access to Health Records Act 1990 lets the personal representative, and anyone who may have a claim arising from the death, apply to the record holder. Northern Ireland has a parallel Order from 1993.

assigned.event: By statute on death: the patient's personal representative, or any person who may have a claim arising out of the death. No appointment is made

starts.event: On the patient's death, by application to the holder of the record

ends.event: No statutory end date. The right lasts while the person remains personal representative or has a possible claim arising from the death

jurisdictions.roleName: Estate administrator exercising Privacy Act rights for a deceased person (federal institutions)
localNames: person authorized ... to administer the estate of that person
jurisdictions.summary: For personal information held by federal government institutions (including health and benefits records), the Privacy Regulations let a person authorized under federal or provincial law to administer a deceased person's estate exercise that person's Privacy Act rights, only for administering the estate. Information about someone dead more than 20 years is not 'personal information' for the use, disclosure and ATIA s 19 rules.

assigned.event: Appointment as estate administrator under provincial law (executor, estate trustee, liquidator, administrator)

starts.event: On authority to administer the estate

ends.event: Estate administration ends (rights exist 'only for the purpose of such administration')
More than 20 years after death: the information is excluded from 'personal information' for Privacy Act ss 7, 8 and 26 and ATIA s 19

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Person who may act for a deceased individual under BC privacy law
jurisdictions.summary: Public bodies such as health authorities fall under FIPPA. There, a committee acting under Patients Property Act s 24, otherwise the personal representative, otherwise the nearest relative, may make access requests and give consents for a deceased adult. Private organizations such as private clinics fall under PIPA. There, the personal representative acts, including an executor named in the will before any grant, otherwise the nearest relative.

assigned.event: Status under statute or regulation at death (committee, personal representative, or nearest relative)

starts.event: At death

ends.event: A higher-ranked person (committee or personal representative) exists or becomes available, or the nearest relative ceases to be willing and able (passes to next)
PIPA: information about someone dead 20 or more years may be disclosed for archival or historical purposes without consent

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Substitute decision-maker for personal health information (PHIPA)
localNames: person who has assumed responsibility for the administration of the deceased's estate
jurisdictions.summary: Under PHIPA, consent about an incapable person's health information goes to a hierarchy that mirrors the HCCA: guardians and attorneys (within their authority), then the Board representative, spouse, and so on. That person can also make access requests. After death, the estate trustee (or whoever has assumed administration if there is none) acts. PHIPA stops applying 50 years after death, or 120 years after the record was created if earlier.

assigned.event: By statute: PHIPA s 26 ranking for an incapable individual; s 23(1) para 4 for a deceased individual

starts.event: When the individual is found incapable of consenting to collection, use or disclosure. For the estate trustee, on death.

ends.event: Individual regains capacity (living SDM)
PHIPA ceases to apply: the earlier of 120 years after record creation and 50 years after death

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Persons entitled to a deceased person's personal or health information
localNames: personne liée à une personne décédée
jurisdictions.summary: Health and social services bodies fall under R-22.1 (S.Q. 2023, c. 5). Heirs, liquidators and beneficiaries get information needed for their role. A spouse or close relative gets information that helps the grieving process, and a spouse or direct relatives get the cause of death, unless the deceased refused in writing. Private enterprises fall under P-39.1 as amended by Law 25 (S.Q. 2021, c. 25). The grieving-process disclosure (s 40.1) applies there too; other access is limited to what affects the requester's rights.

assigned.event: Status at death (heir, liquidator, beneficiary, spouse, close relative, genetic relative)

starts.event: At death; before death, a tutor or homologated mandatary has access to information about an incapable adult held by a health body

ends.event: Liquidator's access tied to the liquidator's rights and obligations; ends with that capacity
Private sector: after 30 years from death (health information 100 years from the document date) information may be communicated without consent

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: HIPAA personal representative
jurisdictions.summary: Federal privacy law does not appoint anyone. A health care provider or health plan must treat a person as the patient for HIPAA purposes, such as getting records or signing authorizations, when state or other law gives that person authority: authority over health-care decisions for a living adult, or authority over the decedent or the estate after death. The role is derived: it starts and ends when the underlying state-law role (health care agent, guardian, parent, executor/administrator) starts and ends. For decedents, protection lasts 50 years after death.

assigned.event: A person gets authority under state or other applicable law (e.g., health care power of attorney, guardianship, parent of a minor, letters as executor/administrator). HIPAA itself does not assign anyone.

starts.event: At the same moment the underlying state-law authority takes effect: authority over health-care decisions (living individual) or authority to act for the decedent or the estate (after death)

ends.event: The underlying state-law authority ends (e.g., a health care agent's authority ends at death, or a guardianship is terminated). Status as a personal representative for a living individual lapses with it.
The authority of the executor, administrator, or other person to act for the decedent or the estate ends under state law
50 years after death: the information is no longer protected health information, so a personal representative has no Privacy Rule rights over it

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: My Health Record authorised representative
jurisdictions.summary: Someone who acts in place of an adult, whom the System Operator is satisfied cannot make decisions, for everything the My Health Records Act allows. It is first a person authorised under Commonwealth, state or territory law or by a court or tribunal (for example an attorney or guardian), otherwise another appropriate person. While one exists, the recipient cannot act for themselves. Also covers parents of children under 14.

assigned.event: System Operator is satisfied the adult is not capable of making decisions and that the person is authorised under law or a court/tribunal decision (or is otherwise appropriate)

starts.event: At the time the System Operator is so satisfied. The representative may then do anything the Act authorises the recipient to do, and must seek out and follow the recipient's will and preferences.

ends.event: The System Operator is no longer satisfied the adult lacks decision-making capacity. Status exists only 'at a time when' the recipient has an authorised representative.
Death of the healthcare recipient: the System Operator must cancel the registration. Uploaded records are kept (not destroyed) until 30 years after death.

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: My Health Record nominated representative
jurisdictions.summary: An individual the healthcare recipient chooses by agreement and notifies to the System Operator. They can act on the record within the limits the recipient sets, alongside (not instead of) the recipient.

assigned.event: Recipient and individual agree the individual will be nominated representative, and the recipient notifies the System Operator

starts.event: While the agreement is in force and has been notified. The recipient may still act personally.

ends.event: Agreement no longer in force (e.g. ended by the recipient or representative)
Death of the healthcare recipient: registration cancelled; records retained until 30 years after death

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Authorised representative under the Health Records and Information Privacy Act
jurisdictions.summary: For NSW health-privacy purposes, an enduring attorney, guardian, person responsible, parent of a child, or other person empowered by law can act for an individual. The scope depends on that underlying role.

assigned.event: Holding one of the listed underlying roles

starts.event: When the underlying authority is in effect (for example, the enduring guardian's appointment takes effect)

ends.event: Underlying authority ends, or acting would be inconsistent with a court or tribunal order

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Authorised representative / legal representative under the Health Records Act 2001
jurisdictions.summary: For a living person who cannot consent or request access, an authorised representative may exercise their Health Records Act rights to the extent needed for the representative's functions. Authorised representatives include a guardian, an enduring attorney, a medical treatment decision maker or an administrator. The Act protects deceased persons for 30 years after death. During that period a legal representative (executor with probate, or administrator) exercises the deceased's rights.

assigned.event: Derived from another role (guardian, enduring attorney, medical treatment decision maker, administrator; after death, executor with probate or administrator)

starts.event: When the individual is incapable of consenting or requesting access (living); on grant of probate or administration (deceased)

ends.event: Underlying authority ends or individual regains capacity
Individual has been dead for more than 30 years: Act no longer applies

roles.label: Heir by universal succession
roles.definition: An heir who takes the estate as a whole at the moment of death, without any grant and without a default executor.

jurisdictions.label: Mauritius
jurisdictions.roleName: Héritier (saisine)
jurisdictions.summary: No grant and no intermediate office: the heirs are seised of the deceased’s property, rights and actions of right, subject to the obligation to discharge all the charges of the succession. The State, by contrast, must be put in possession by the court.

assigned.event: Death of the deceased

starts.event: Heirs are seised of plein droit of the property, rights and actions of the deceased, bound to discharge the charges of the succession

ends.event: Succession liquidated and partitioned

jurisdictions.label: Rwanda
jurisdictions.roleName: Heir
jurisdictions.summary: Succession opens on death at the deceased’s domicile or residence, and from that day a person entitled by will or by law is called an heir — but only for as long as they accept it. Where someone has disappeared, succession opens instead on a final declaratory judgement of death.

assigned.event: Succession opens on the death of a person, at their domicile or residence

starts.event: From the day of the opening of succession the person entitled by will or by law is called an heir, as long as they accept it

ends.event: Estate liquidated and the liquidator’s acts approved by the succession council

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Heir (继承人)
jurisdictions.summary: Succession begins at the moment the decedent dies. An heir who wants out must say so in writing before the estate is dealt with; saying nothing counts as acceptance. A legatee, by contrast, must accept within sixty days of learning of the legacy or is taken to have renounced.

assigned.event: Succession begins on the death of the decedent; the estate is the lawful property they leave

starts.event: Statutory succession applies, or a will, legacy or legacy-support agreement where there is one; an heir who does not renounce in writing before the estate is dealt with is taken to have accepted

ends.event: The heir renounces in writing before the estate is dealt with
The estate administrator divides the estate under the will or as the law provides

jurisdictions.label: Japan
jurisdictions.roleName: Heir (相続人)
jurisdictions.summary: No grant: inheritance commences by death and the heir succeeds from that moment to every right and duty that belonged to the decedent’s property, except what was purely personal to them. The heir has three months from learning of the commencement to accept simply, accept with limitation, or renounce.

assigned.event: Inheritance commences by death

starts.event: From the time inheritance commences the heir succeeds to all rights and duties attaching to the decedent’s property, except those personal to the decedent

ends.event: Simple or qualified acceptance, or renunciation, within three months of learning of the commencement; the Family Court may extend that period

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Heir
jurisdictions.summary: Korea has no grant of representation: inheritance commences by death and the heir succeeds to the blanket rights and duties of the estate from that moment. The heir has three months from learning of the commencement to accept absolutely, accept with limitation, or renounce.

assigned.event: Inheritance is commenced by death

starts.event: The heir succeeds to the blanket rights and duties of the estate from the time inheritance commences, with no grant

ends.event: Renunciation within three months of learning of the commencement, or the period passes with absolute acceptance

jurisdictions.label: Denmark
jurisdictions.roleName: Arving
jurisdictions.summary: The nearest heirs are the children, sharing equally. Where the heirs all ask and the estate can cover its debts, the estate is released to them for private administration.

assigned.event: By the statutory order of succession or by will

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Estate released to a bobestyrer instead, or administration completed

jurisdictions.label: Finland
jurisdictions.roleName: Kuolinpesän osakas

citation.cite: Code of Inheritance 40/1965 ch 18 s 1 (amendments up to 1228/2001)
citation.title: Code of Inheritance (unofficial translation published on Finlex)
citation.quote: The heirs, the universal beneficiaries under a testament and the surviving spouse shall be shareholders in the decedent's estate.

jurisdictions.summary: The heirs, universal legatees and surviving spouse are the parties to the estate and, absent special administration, must administer it jointly.

assigned.event: By status as heir, universal legatee or surviving spouse

starts.event: On death

ends.event: Estate handed to a pesänselvittäjä, or wound up

jurisdictions.label: France
jurisdictions.roleName: Héritier
jurisdictions.summary: Succession is universal and automatic: heirs designated by law are seised of right of the deceased's goods, rights and actions. Failing heirs and universal legatees, the estate goes to the State, which must apply to be sent into possession.

assigned.event: Heirship by law, or universal legatee or donee under the will

starts.event: At death, of right — no grant and no court step

ends.event: Succession settled and divided

jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Erbe (Gesamtrechtsnachfolger)
jurisdictions.summary: German law has no default executor: on death the whole estate, including digital assets, passes automatically and immediately to the heirs as universal successors.

assigned.event: By will or by the statutory order of succession

starts.event: Automatically at the moment of death — no grant or court act required

ends.event: Estate distributed; Erbengemeinschaft wound up

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Heir (erede)
jurisdictions.summary: Succession opens at the moment of death, at the deceased’s last domicile. The estate is devolved by law or by will, but it is acquired by acceptance — and acceptance, once made, relates back to the moment succession opened. Acceptance may be pure and simple or with the benefit of inventory, which keeps the heir’s own property separate from the estate’s debts.

assigned.event: Succession opens at the moment of death, at the place of the deceased’s last domicile, and is devolved by law or by will

starts.event: The estate is acquired by acceptance, whose effect relates back to the moment succession opened; acceptance may be pure and simple or with the benefit of inventory

ends.event: Where the person called has not accepted and is not in possession of estate assets, the court appoints a curator of the vacant estate

jurisdictions.label: Netherlands
jurisdictions.roleName: Erfgenaam
jurisdictions.summary: Dutch succession is universal and automatic. At the moment of death the heirs step into the deceased's transmissible rights, possession and holdership of right, and become debtors of the debts that survive the death. There is no grant.

assigned.event: Heirship by will or by intestacy

starts.event: At death, of right — no grant, no appointment and no court step

ends.event: Estate divided among those entitled

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law

citation.title: Heir and legatee (unofficial translation published by the Ministry of Justice; law as of 6 Oct 2015)
citation.quote: A person who succeeds pursuant to universal title shall be called heir

jurisdictions.summary: Rights to the succession transmit from the moment of death and the heirs succeed to all the deceased's rights and obligations by the mere fact of that death.

assigned.event: By will or by law

starts.event: At the moment of death

ends.event: Estate partitioned

starts.event: On death, where no separate administration is arranged

ends.event: Estate handed to a boutredningsman, or the estate is wound up

jurisdictions.label: Mexico — federal law
jurisdictions.roleName: Heredero
jurisdictions.summary: Inheritance is succession in all the deceased's property, rights and obligations that death does not extinguish. On death the heirs acquire a right to the hereditary mass as a common patrimony until it is divided.

assigned.event: By will or by law

starts.event: On death, as a right to the hereditary mass held in common

ends.event: Division of the hereditary mass

jurisdictions.label: Argentina
jurisdictions.roleName: Heredero
jurisdictions.summary: Death opens the succession and transmits the estate. Descendants, ascendants and the spouse are invested as heirs from the day of death with no formality and no judicial intervention, even if unaware; collateral and testamentary heirs must be invested by the succession judge.

assigned.event: Real or presumed death opens the succession and transmits the estate to those called by will or by law

starts.event: Descendants, ascendants and spouse are invested from the day of death without formality or judicial intervention; collaterals and testamentary heirs are invested by the judge

ends.event: Renunciation, or the right to accept lapsing ten years after the succession opens, the heir then being treated as renouncing

jurisdictions.label: Brazil
jurisdictions.roleName: Herdeiro
jurisdictions.summary: On the opening of the succession the inheritance passes at once to the legitimate and testamentary heirs, without any grant or court act.

assigned.event: By law or by will

starts.event: Immediately on the opening of the succession, that is on death

ends.event: Partition homologated

nameEn.en: Person charged with executing post-mortem data directives

jurisdictions.summary: France lets a person say in advance what happens to their personal data after death, and name someone to carry that out. General directives may be lodged with a CNIL-certified digital trusted third party; particular ones go to the controller and need specific consent that cannot come from accepting terms of service.

ends.event: Directives modified or revoked by the person at any time

jurisdictions.label: China
jurisdictions.roleName: Agent under a mandate (委托代理人)
jurisdictions.summary: Ordinary agency by authorisation. Where the authorisation is in writing it must state the agent, the matters, the scope and the period, and be signed or sealed by the principal. Article 173 lists what ends it, including the death of either party; the principal’s loss of capacity is not among the listed events, and the Code’s express mechanism for authority meant to operate after capacity is lost is the advance-appointed guardianship of art 33.

assigned.event: The principal authorises the agent; a written authorisation states the agent, the matters, the scope and the period, signed or sealed by the principal

starts.event: The agent acts within the authority conferred

ends.event: The period expires or the business is completed
The principal revokes the mandate, or the agent resigns it
The agent loses capacity for civil conduct
Death of the agent or of the principal

jurisdictions.label: India
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under a power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An ordinary power. India has no durable financial power by default: the agency is terminated by either the principal or the agent dying or becoming of unsound mind.

assigned.event: Principal executes an instrument empowering a person to act in their name

starts.event: On execution of the instrument

ends.event: Principal revokes, agent renounces, or the business of the agency is completed
Either the principal or the agent dies or becomes of unsound mind, or the principal is adjudicated insolvent

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandatary under an ordinary mandate
jurisdictions.summary: The ordinary agency relationship. It is not a durable instrument: it ends on the death or bankruptcy of either party, and also if the mandatary is placed under adult guardianship.

assigned.event: Mandate entrusts the mandatary with the management of affairs, and the mandatary accepts

starts.event: On acceptance of the mandate

ends.event: Death or bankruptcy of either party, or the mandatary is adjudged to commence adult guardianship

jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandatario (mandato ordinario)
jurisdictions.summary: An ordinary mandate. It ends on the grantor's death and also when representative curatela is established for them.

assigned.event: Grant of mandate

starts.event: On grant

ends.event: Revocation, death or insolvency of either party, or establishment of representative curatela

jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an ordinary (general) power of attorney
localNames: donee of a power of attorney
general power of attorney (Powers of Attorney Act 1971 s 10)
jurisdictions.summary: An ordinary power of attorney under the Powers of Attorney Act 1971 and the common law of agency. It needs no registration and can be used at once, but it stops working when the donor loses mental capacity and ends on the donor's death. The 1971 Act protects attorneys and third parties who act without knowing it has been revoked.

assigned.event: Donor with capacity executes a power of attorney by deed

starts.event: On execution, or as the instrument states

ends.event: Donor loses mental capacity (common-law revocation; 'you can only use this while they have mental capacity')
Donor dies
Donor revokes, or the instrument's stated period expires

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under an ordinary (general) power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A non-enduring power of attorney stops working when the donor becomes mentally incapable of managing their affairs.

assigned.event: Donor grants power of attorney

starts.event: As the instrument provides

ends.event: Donor becomes mentally incapable of managing affairs
Donor dies

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Attorney under a general (non-enduring) power of attorney
jurisdictions.summary: A general power of attorney under Part 1 of the Power of Attorney Act (short forms 1 and 2) lets an attorney do anything the donor can lawfully do by an attorney. It is not an enduring power of attorney, so it ends if the donor becomes mentally incapable, and also on death or revocation. Part 1 protects agents and third parties who act without knowing the authority has ended.

assigned.event: Donor signs a general power of attorney (Form 1 or 2 or other form)

starts.event: On signing, subject to any conditions in the document

ends.event: Donor becomes mentally incapable (not an enduring power of attorney)
Donor dies or revokes
Donor declared a patient by the court under the Patients Property Act

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec
jurisdictions.roleName: Mandatary under an ordinary mandate (power of attorney)
jurisdictions.summary: An ordinary contract of mandate (art 2130) lets the mandatary represent the mandator in juridical acts. It ends on revocation, renunciation, bankruptcy or the death of either party. The mandator's incapacity is NOT listed as an automatic cause: the Code says the mandate 'may' end 'in certain cases' when tutorship is instituted or a protection mandate is homologated, and it continues during homologation proceedings unless the court revokes it.

assigned.event: Mandator confers mandate (contract accepted by mandatary)

starts.event: On acceptance of the mandate

ends.event: Death of mandator or mandatary
Revocation by mandator or renunciation by mandatary
Bankruptcy of either party
In certain cases, institution of tutorship or homologation of a protection mandate for the mandator; court may revoke for serious reason during homologation proceedings

assigned.event: Grantor confers a mandate

starts.event: On the grant

ends.event: Revocation; renunciation by the mandatary; death of either party; interdiction

jurisdictions.label: Japan
jurisdictions.roleName: Assistant (補助人)
jurisdictions.summary: The lightest tier, for a person whose capacity is insufficient without being markedly so. Its distinguishing feature is consent: where anyone other than the person applies, the adjudication cannot be made without that person’s own agreement.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates the commencement of assistance where capacity is insufficient, except where the grounds for guardianship or curatorship apply

starts.event: On the adjudication; where the application is made by anyone other than the person, their own consent is required

ends.event: Death of the person, which commences the inheritance

jurisdictions.label: South Korea
jurisdictions.roleName: Specific guardian
jurisdictions.summary: Support for one matter or one period, and the only Korean guardianship that cannot be imposed over the principal’s objection. Representation is optional and time- and scope-limited when the court grants it.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of specific guardianship, fixing the period or the scope of affairs

starts.event: Court may confer a right of representation on the specific guardian for a set period and scope, and may require the supervisor’s consent to its exercise

ends.event: The fixed period expires or the specified affairs are completed
Death of the principal

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Decision-making assistant
jurisdictions.summary: The lightest tier of the 2015 Act. The person keeps the decision; the assistant helps them gather information and express a choice. No registration and no court involvement.

assigned.event: Person whose capacity is or may shortly be in question appoints an assistant in a decision-making assistance agreement

starts.event: On the agreement taking effect; the appointer retains the decision throughout

ends.event: Agreement revoked, assistant becomes ineligible or is disqualified
Death of the appointer

jurisdictions.label: Ireland
jurisdictions.roleName: Co-decision-maker
jurisdictions.summary: The middle tier. Decisions are made jointly with the appointer, and unlike the assistant tier the agreement must be registered with the Decision Support Service before it has effect.

assigned.event: Person whose capacity is or may shortly be in question appoints a suitable person to make decisions jointly with them

starts.event: On registration of the co-decision-making agreement with the Director of the Decision Support Service

ends.event: Agreement revoked or removed from the Register
Death of the appointer

jurisdictions.label: Italy
jurisdictions.roleName: Support administrator (amministratore di sostegno)
jurisdictions.summary: The measure that made Italy’s 2004 reform notable. It is calibrated rather than all-or-nothing: the beneficiary keeps capacity for every act the decree does not reserve to exclusive representation or assistance, and may always perform acts of daily life. The decree fixes the administrator’s object and duration, and the administrator must have regard to the beneficiary’s needs and aspirations and keep them informed.

assigned.event: A person who, through infirmity or physical or mental impairment, cannot see to their own interests — even partly or temporarily — may be assisted; the application may be brought by the person themselves, among others

starts.event: The giudice tutelare appoints by decree within sixty days, stating its duration and the acts the administrator may do in the beneficiary’s name or together with them

ends.event: The measure is revoked on application by the beneficiary, the administrator, the public prosecutor or others entitled, when the conditions for it have ceased
Acts done in breach of law or beyond the object or powers conferred may be annulled on application

assigned.event: By fact, without appointment

starts.event: When the person in fact provides support

ends.event: Death, or a sufficient formal support measure replaces it

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Representative under a section 7 (standard) representation agreement
jurisdictions.summary: BC's supported decision-making tool. An adult can make a section 7 agreement even if unable to make a contract. It authorizes a representative to help the adult decide, or to decide for the adult, about personal care, routine finances, most health care and legal services. It cannot cover refusing life-preserving care. It takes effect on execution and ends on death.

assigned.event: Adult signs a s 7 agreement; the capacity test weighs relationship of trust and expressed wishes rather than contractual capacity

starts.event: On execution (all signatures, witnesses and certificates), unless a later triggering event is specified

ends.event: Adult dies
Revocation, court cancellation, or representative's death, resignation or incapability
Routine financial provisions cancelled on bankruptcy of the adult or representative, a receiver's appointment, or the representative's conviction for dishonesty

localNames: assistant to a person of full age
jurisdictions.summary: Created by S.Q. 2020, c. 11, in force 1 November 2022. A person of full age who has a difficulty asks the Public Curator to recognize one or two assistants to help with decisions and act as intermediary with third parties. The person keeps full legal capacity, and the assistant cannot sign for them. Recognition is entered in a public register and lasts 3 years unless it ends sooner.

assigned.event: Joint application by the person and proposed assistant to the Public Curator (or via a certified advocate or notary); notice to 2 family members or interested persons with 30-day objection period

starts.event: Public Curator recognizes the assistant and enters it in the public register

ends.event: Expiry of three years, or earlier at the person's request
Tutorship instituted or protection mandate homologated for the assisted person or the assistant, or temporary representative designated for the assistant (on notice to the Public Curator)
Assistant ceases to act
Public Curator terminates recognition for serious reason to fear injury (reviewable by court within 30 days)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Supportive attorney
jurisdictions.summary: An adult with capacity can appoint a supportive attorney. The supportive attorney helps the principal make and carry out the principal's own decisions on personal, financial or other matters, but not medical treatment. They may get information, communicate decisions and take steps to give effect to them. The appointment has no effect while the principal lacks capacity and is revoked at death.

assigned.event: Adult principal with capacity signs the appointment form; supportive attorney signs a witnessed acceptance

starts.event: On the time, circumstance or occasion specified; otherwise on making

ends.event: Principal lacks decision-making capacity for the matters: appointment has no effect for that period
Death of principal
Revocation by principal (with capacity); death, incapacity, insolvency, care-provider status or dishonesty conviction of the supportive attorney; resignation; VCAT order

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Support person (medical treatment)
jurisdictions.summary: Any person with decision-making capacity, including a child, may appoint one support person. The support person helps them make, communicate and carry out their own medical treatment decisions. The support person represents their interests, including when they lack capacity, but cannot make treatment decisions.

assigned.event: Person with capacity signs a witnessed appointment; support person accepts

starts.event: On the date the appointment is made

ends.event: Revocation by the person (with capacity) or a later appointment of a support person
Resignation or VCAT revocation
Death of the person (no express provision)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — Victoria
jurisdictions.roleName: Supportive guardian or supportive administrator appointed by VCAT
jurisdictions.summary: VCAT may appoint a supportive guardian or supportive administrator if the person consents and would have decision-making capacity with practicable and appropriate support. The appointee may get information, communicate decisions and give effect to the person's decisions, but does not decide for them. Orders are reassessed like substitute orders.

assigned.event: VCAT makes a supportive guardianship or supportive administration order, with the person's consent

starts.event: On the making of the order

ends.event: A later guardianship or administration order is made (ceases to the extent of inconsistency)
VCAT revokes on reassessment
Death of the supported person (appointee must report death; no express lapse provision)

jurisdictions.label: Argentina
jurisdictions.roleName: Persona de apoyo
jurisdictions.summary: Argentina’s default response to impaired capacity is support, not substitution. A support measure may be judicial or extrajudicial, and its stated purpose is to promote autonomy and facilitate the person’s own communication, understanding and expression of will.

assigned.event: Judge restricts capacity for specified acts and designates one or more support persons, or a support is arranged extrajudicially

starts.event: The judgment sets the extent and scope of the restriction and specifies the functions and acts limited, keeping the intrusion on personal autonomy as small as possible

ends.event: Death of the person

jurisdictions.summary: A person with a disability chooses at least two trusted supporters to help them decide on civil matters, keeping the decision their own rather than transferring it.

assigned.event: The person elects at least two trusted supporters

starts.event: On the supported decision-making arrangement taking effect

ends.event: Death of the person

assigned.event: By holding the office of legal representative or asset administrator

starts.event: On taking up the administration

ends.event: Administration ends

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Personal representative dealing with HMRC for a deceased person
jurisdictions.summary: HMRC deals with the executor or administrator. By statute they are liable for income tax owed by the deceased, and for inheritance tax on the free estate, and they must file returns for both the deceased's final period and the estate's administration period. Tax law does not create a separate appointment: the role follows the person's status as personal representative under succession law.

assigned.event: Person becomes executor (named in will) or administrator (grant of letters of administration) under the law of the relevant UK jurisdiction

starts.event: From death (executor) or grant (administrator), as succession law provides; HMRC may issue a return for the deceased's pre-death income

ends.event: Estate tax affairs settled after the administration period. HMRC cannot assess PRs for the deceased's pre-death income or gains more than 4 years after the end of the tax year of death

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Legal representative of a deceased taxpayer (CRA)
jurisdictions.summary: The Income Tax Act defines a deceased taxpayer's legal representative as the executor, administrator, liquidator, heir or similar fiduciary dealing with the estate. That person files the final return (due by the later of the normal due date and six months after death, for deaths after October). They must get a clearance certificate before distributing property, or they are personally liable for unpaid tax.

assigned.event: Appointment under provincial law (executor named in a will, court-appointed administrator/estate trustee, Quebec liquidator). The CRA registers the person on receiving the death certificate and the will, grant or letters, or Form RC552 if there is no will.

starts.event: On death. The statutory filing duty falls on the legal representatives. CRA access to the deceased's tax records follows once the documents are processed.

ends.event: Tax liabilities settled and a clearance certificate obtained before final distribution. Distributing without one makes the representative personally liable up to the value distributed.
The provincial fiduciary office ends (removal, renunciation, replacement). CRA representation follows the underlying appointment.

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Legal representative of a living taxpayer who cannot act (CRA)
jurisdictions.summary: If an individual cannot file their own return, the Income Tax Act lets their guardian, committee or other legal representative file it. The CRA recognises as legal representative a person appointed by a legal document: a court-appointed guardian, trustee or committee, a person named in a power of attorney, or a representative under a BC-style representation agreement. The authority comes from, and ends with, that provincial instrument.

assigned.event: Provincial instrument or order: power of attorney, representation agreement, or court appointment as guardian/trustee/committee

jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario
jurisdictions.roleName: Legal representative of a deceased taxpayer (CRA)
jurisdictions.summary: The Income Tax Act defines a deceased taxpayer's legal representative as the executor, administrator, liquidator, heir or similar fiduciary dealing with the estate. That person files the final return (due by the later of the normal due date and six months after death, for deaths after October). They must get a clearance certificate before distributing property, or they are personally liable for unpaid tax.

assigned.event: Appointment under provincial law (executor named in a will, court-appointed administrator/estate trustee, Quebec liquidator). The CRA registers the person on receiving the death certificate and the will, grant or letters, or Form RC552 if there is no will.

ends.event: Tax liabilities settled and a clearance certificate obtained before final distribution. Distributing without one makes the representative personally liable up to the value distributed.
