jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: Fiduciary of record with the IRS (Form 56 notice)
jurisdictions.summary: Federal tax law does not create fiduciary authority. It recognizes a fiduciary (guardian, conservator, executor, administrator, trustee, or anyone else acting in a fiduciary capacity) once that person notifies the IRS, usually on Form 56. From then on, the fiduciary stands in the taxpayer's shoes for tax matters until notice is given that the fiduciary capacity has terminated. That IRS-facing status can therefore outlast the state-law appointment until termination is reported. An agent under a power of attorney is not a fiduciary for this purpose and uses Form 2848 instead.

assigned.event: Person begins acting for another in a fiduciary capacity under other law (e.g., court appointment as guardian or conservator, letters testamentary or of administration, or trusteeship)

starts.event: Notice of the fiduciary relationship is filed with the IRS (Form 56)

ends.event: Notice is given to the IRS that the fiduciary capacity has terminated (Form 56, Part II)

jurisdictions.label: Australia — New South Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Legal personal representative (LPR) of a deceased estate for tax
localNames: trustee of the deceased person's estate
jurisdictions.summary: The executor with a grant of probate, or the administrator with letters of administration, whom the ATO deals with as if they were the deceased. They lodge the date-of-death return and estate trust returns and pay the deceased's tax out of the estate. Without a grant, the ATO will help but will not record the person as the authorised LPR.

assigned.event: Named as executor in a will, or appointed administrator by a Supreme Court (state/territory law)

starts.event: On grant of probate or letters of administration and notifying the ATO with the grant; the ATO then records the person as authorised LPR

ends.event: Tax obligations of the deceased and estate discharged and estate distributed (no statutory discharge event in the tax Acts)

jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales
jurisdictions.roleName: Appointee for armed forces compensation / war pension
localNames: person appointed to act for M (AFCS art 71)
administration of pension by the Secretary of State (SPO art 49)
jurisdictions.summary: Armed forces compensation has its own appointment power, separate from DWP. Under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme the Secretary of State (Defence) may appoint someone to act for a person who is incapable of managing their affairs 'by reason of mental infirmity', if no one else has legal authority. For older war pensions the Secretary of State can administer the pension directly.

assigned.event: Secretary of State appoints in writing a person (18+ if an individual). The Secretary of State must consider the person incapable of managing their affairs by reason of mental infirmity, and no one else may have legal authority to act

starts.event: On written appointment

ends.event: Secretary of State revokes (and may appoint another)
Appointee resigns with one month's written notice
Death of the beneficiary (not stated expressly in art 71)

jurisdictions.label: Canada — British Columbia
jurisdictions.roleName: Administrator of a Pension Act award for an incapable recipient (Veterans Affairs Canada)
localNames: person or agency selected by the Minister
jurisdictions.summary: Under the Pension Act, if a person entitled to an award appears to the Minister to be incapable of managing their own affairs, the Minister may direct that the award be administered for them by the Department or by a person or agency the Minister selects. No equivalent provision was found in the Veterans Well-being Act or its Regulations.

assigned.event: Minister directs administration of the award because it appears the recipient cannot manage their own affairs because of infirmity, illness or other cause

starts.event: On the Minister's direction

ends.event: Recipient dies: the award stops, and amounts paid after the last day of the month of death can be recovered from survivor awards
ends.note: Section 83(5) implies awards stop after the month of death. No express 'administration ends on death' text was found.

ends.event: The Minister revokes or changes the direction (e.g. the recipient regains capacity)

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal
jurisdictions.roleName: VA fiduciary
jurisdictions.summary: An individual or entity that the Department of Veterans Affairs appoints to receive and manage a beneficiary's VA benefits. VA appoints one after a VA rating authority finds the beneficiary unable to manage VA benefits, after a court finds the beneficiary unable to manage financial affairs, or when the beneficiary is a minor. The VA incompetency rating is an administrative decision, with notice and a hearing right, and doubt is resolved in favor of competency. The role ends through removal by the VA Hub Manager: when VA rates the beneficiary competent, when the beneficiary dies, when a successor is appointed, or when the fiduciary is removed for cause or withdraws with VA's permission.

assigned.event: VA rating authority rates the beneficiary incompetent to handle VA funds, or a court with jurisdiction finds the beneficiary unable to manage financial affairs. The Hub Manager then investigates and appoints a fiduciary.

starts.event: Hub Manager appoints the fiduciary; VA pays benefits to the fiduciary for the use and benefit of the beneficiary and dependents

ends.event: Beneficiary dies: this is a listed reason for removal, and VA benefits are discontinued as of the last day of the month before death
VA rating authority determines the beneficiary can manage VA benefits (or a court finds this, if the court order was the basis)
Removal for fiduciary reasons (misuse, failure to account, bar under 13.130, loss of qualifications, etc.), or withdrawal after VA arranges a successor

jurisdictions.summary: An individual or entity that the Department of Veterans Affairs appoints to receive and manage a beneficiary's VA benefits. VA appoints one after a VA rating authority finds the beneficiary unable to manage VA benefits, after a court finds the beneficiary unable to manage financial affairs, or when the beneficiary is a minor. The VA incompetency rating is an administrative decision, with notice and a hearing right, and doubt is resolved in favor of competency. The role ends through removal by the VA Hub Manager: when VA rates the beneficiary competent, when the beneficiary dies, when a successor is appointed, or when the fiduciary is removed for cause or withdraws with VA's permission.

assigned.event: VA rating authority rates the beneficiary incompetent to handle VA funds, or a court with jurisdiction finds the beneficiary unable to manage financial affairs. The Hub Manager then investigates and appoints a fiduciary.

starts.event: Hub Manager appoints the fiduciary; VA pays benefits to the fiduciary for the use and benefit of the beneficiary and dependents

ends.event: Beneficiary dies: this is a listed reason for removal, and VA benefits are discontinued as of the last day of the month before death
VA rating authority determines the beneficiary can manage VA benefits (or a court finds this, if the court order was the basis)
Removal for fiduciary reasons (misuse, failure to account, bar under 13.130, loss of qualifications, etc.), or withdrawal after VA arranges a successor
